a1-fixed-objective-maximizer.author: @smithy-verity
a1-fixed-objective-maximizer.notes:
Shared by the informal route and the anti-naturality root. The table holds the
two trained-policy pictures of the landed filing, three published pictures
the content stage of 2026-10-05 added (Grace's weak pseudo-agents, Shah's
coherence without a convergent goal, Thornley's incomplete preferences), and a
residual. Statement unchanged; the partition leaf's Statement names the new
rows and carries the version bump.

Whether the fixed-objective reconstruction and the complete-fixed-preferences
reconstruction are one assumption is open; the identification is the filing
session's.
a1-fixed-objective-maximizer.source:
Reconstructed from Omohundro 2008, section 2: "Because they are goal directed,
they will try to change themselves to better meet their goals in the future",
and section 3: "these systems will try to be rational by representing their
preferences using utility functions whose expectations they try to maximize";
and from Bostrom 2012, section 2, which takes instrumental reasoning toward a
final goal as the meaning of intelligence.

Identified with the assumption of Soares, Fallenstein, Yudkowsky and Armstrong
2015, Corrigibility, footnote 1: "Von Neumann-Morgenstern rational agents (von
Neumann and Morgenstern 1944), that is, agents which attempt to maximize
expected utility according to some utility function." Neither source states the
assumption in this form.
a1-fixed-objective-maximizer.statement:
The system selects actions by their predicted consequences for a single
objective that is fixed across the episode.

picture's scope; the three added pictures are drawn from the published
critiques and worded so that each excludes the trained-policy rows (a designed
agent; a utility over action histories; a non-maximizing single objective).
a1-fixed-objective-maximizer.partition.source:
Turner 2024 and Krakovna and Kramar 2023 as read for the two trained-policy
pictures; Grace 2022, Shah 2018 and Thornley 2024 and 2025 for the three
published critiques; the residual row covers every other kind of system.
a1-fixed-objective-maximizer.partition.statement:
The pictures under a1-fixed-objective-maximizer, a trained policy with a
learned goal from the training-compatible set, a trained policy with no single
objective, a weak pseudo-agent that takes only some effective opportunities for
its objective, a coherent agent whose utility is over action histories, a
designed agent with incomplete preferences across trajectory lengths, and the
residual, are exclusive and exhaustive.

abstraction-arc.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

frame.question: Which work on abstraction, logical induction and agency gives the program a representation theorem for logical inductors, a decision theory set in that representation, and a notion of scale-free agency that covers cooperative equilibria?

abstraction-arc.notes:
A programme filed as a sub-frame of the-program, as the roadmap's later
stages. Its roots are the roadmap's Stages 4, 5 and 6 as sub-frames, the
ledger-logic line as a sub-frame (Stage 3 material by content, assigned to this
programme by the round), the want for a mathematics of the intentional stance,
the embedded-agency question from li-deference.md, and two cruxes that re-rank
the stages. The decomposition is the filing session's reading of the roadmap,
not a list the roadmap gives.

The roadmap orders the stages ("first… then… then…") and also says the mastery
program "runs in parallel with everything"; the crux mastery-gates-stage5 holds
that tension. Within the sub-frame the classes, the outside option and the
undescribed-failure valuation are the top frame's.
abstraction-arc.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/roadmap.md, Stage 5: "a theory
combining abstraction with logical induction in a natural way, and a
representation theorem about when it is natural to interpret something as a
logical inductor"; Stage 6: "The Stage-5 object has a claim to being the right
setting to do decision theory in" and "A notion of scale-free agency based on a
solid theory of the abstraction of agency"; "A characterization of approximate
cooperative equilibria as agents, with meaningful advice about how to steer
towards such equilibria".
abstraction-arc.statement:
A theory of abstraction compatible with logical induction yields a
representation theorem stating when a system is interpretable as a logical
inductor, a decision theory formulated in that setting, and a notion of
scale-free agency under which approximate cooperative equilibria are agents.

A coarsening of a decision-determined agent, in FAF's abstract

abstraction-theories-integration.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
abstraction-theories-integration.notes:
A mid-level plan of Stage 4, filed as an and because its Statement names the
three relations as its parts; the choice of the three theories is the filing
session's. Steve Petersen (abstraction) is not Sami Petersen, whose 2023 note
on incomplete preferences is in the corrigibility references.
abstraction-theories-integration.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/roadmap.md, Stage 5 ("Having
thoroughly explored existing theories of abstraction (and many variations)").
abstraction-theories-integration.statement:
Petersen's theory of abstraction, Wentworth's natural abstraction and natural
latents, and Eisenstat's condensation are related precisely: Petersen's theory
to Wentworth's, natural latents to condensation, and Petersen's theory to
condensation, each relation stated as a reduction or a complementarity.

abstraction-theories-integration.complet.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
abstraction-theories-integration.complet.source:

fourth pairing (natural latents to Petersen's theory) would pass through one of
the three.
abstraction-theories-integration.complet.statement:
No relation beyond Petersen to Wentworth, natural latents to condensation, and
Petersen to condensation is needed for the three theories to be related
precisely.

could still be wrong about some things" (Demski, Market Truth, LessWrong,
2025-11-24, section Evidence). The crux internal-standard-never-settled
carries the alternatives.
acceleration-only-thesis.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/legitimacy-theory-v1.md, section
2.2, the block quote headed "Acceleration-only thesis"; its own falsifier is

acceleration-only-thesis.statement:
Within the endpoint-preservation framework the only legitimate uplift on
never-settled questions is speed: an advisor that moves the human's endpoint on
the undecidable fragment counts as corruption.

acts-of-war-as-re-bargains.notes:

acts-of-war-as-re-bargains.source:
The filing session's definition, in the vocabulary of Nash bargaining (a
disagreement point, a feasible set) and of the aggregate logical inductor
(aggregate-logical-inductor): a re-bargain the other members did not consent
to, from a position the actor produced, is the case a legitimacy notion for the
coalition has to classify, and the definition classifies it as illegitimate.
acts-of-war-as-re-bargains.statement:
An act of war in the coalition is a unilateral, unconsented re-bargain from a
disagreement point, feasible set or membership the actor produced; moving
weight outside settlement is its symptom, and a planted dogmatic belief is a
weight coup through settlement.

agency-correspondence-refuted.notes:

condensation of both, which the corpus never verified for agents.

uniform worlds with `Pol₂ = (Pol₁, one more bit of behaviour)`. Eisenstat's
Theorem 4.15 needs perfect condensation of both models".
agency-correspondence-refuted.statement:
Under determination of actions by policy and observation and recoverability of
the policy from behaviour alone, two agency attributions to the same behaviour
need not agree on the policy; agreement needs perfect condensation of both
models.

The declaration's four-world witness is a counterexample to the corpus's

and recoverability conditions as its hypotheses.

aggregate-decision-layer-missing.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
aggregate-decision-layer-missing.source:
Critch 2017, Toward Negotiable Reinforcement Learning (the Pareto-optimal
policy uses each member's own beliefs, with weights shifting by each member's
predictive success), set against aggregate-logical-inductor: the market
supplies prices, not a policy, and a policy that maximizes expected utility
under the aggregate's prices is the futarchy form, which Critch's theorem does
not cover. An AI derivation in prose; no proof is in this repository.
aggregate-decision-layer-missing.statement:
No logical-induction market supplies the coalition's decision layer: a
Critch-faithful policy uses each member's own expectation with the aggregate as
bookmaker, while using the aggregate's expectation is the futarchy form and
leaves Pareto optimality.

projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/deference-trust-lab/AGENDA.md, Fast
Student, Slow Teacher (Merging Logical Inductors): a way to build a new
logical inductor combining the strengths of both, fast and aligned. The
aggregate construction is aggregate-logical-inductor's Statement.
aggregate-inductor-is-merging-inductors.statement:
The aggregate logical inductor of aggregate-logical-inductor and the
fast-student, slow-teacher construction, a new inductor combining a trusted
slow one and an untrusted fast one, are two instances of one question: when a
combination of inductors is itself an inductor that a member endorses.

aggregate-logical-inductor.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
aggregate-logical-inductor.notes:
Derived in prose by agents, with no Lean and no human reading; no proof is in
this repository. The Kelly identity and the cancellation are finite algebra
and cheap to check in Lean, which is the given parent.
aggregate-logical-inductor.source:
Garrabrant et al. 2016, Logical Induction (the fixed-point market and its
trading firm); Critch 2017, Toward Negotiable Reinforcement Learning (the
weight path); the claim identifies Critch's weight path with the Kelly
wealth-share path inside the market.
aggregate-logical-inductor.statement:
Members entering the logical-induction paper's fixed-point market as
Kelly-demand traders with every budget, beside the enumerable trading firm,
yield a logical inductor over the union of the members' deductive processes,
and on the settled fragment its normalized member weights follow Critch's
weight path whatever else trades.

aggregate-logical-inductor.improvable.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

fields.reality: a human–AI coalition with learning members, private information and enforcement

aggregate-logical-inductor.improvable.source:
Ruling 35 (the form). The routes are the filing session's list of what the
market picture of aggregate-logical-inductor leaves out: a dynamic weight law,
a disclosure regime, a decision layer, literal exit and a maintained cap.
aggregate-logical-inductor.improvable.statement:
The coalition-as-market picture of the aggregate logical inductor can be
improved until it reflects a human–AI coalition with learning members, private
information and enforcement well.

aggregate-logical-inductor.residual.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
aggregate-logical-inductor.residual.statement:
Some refinement of the coalition-as-market picture not described by the named
routes reflects a human–AI coalition with learning members, private information
and enforcement.

anticipation-branchwise-dominance.author: @smithy-verity
anticipation-branchwise-dominance.notes:
Formal result in leaf form, for act-independent credences; the evidence parent
of the meta-revision question.

Superseded by anticipation-branchwise-dominance--corrigibility-risk, the four-file formal result (record, setting,
bridge, completeness) a second session filed for the same declarations; this
one-sentence form is kept because its estimate event is history.
anticipation-branchwise-dominance.statement:
An agent deferring to the future legitimate evaluation complies at every
credence over revision branches if and only if compliance is weakly preferred
in each branch; otherwise a confident enough anticipation, correct or mistaken,
makes it violate.

anticipation-branchwise-dominance--corri.statement:
An agent that defers to the future legitimate evaluation complies at every

general quantitative question is open.
approx-introspection-quantitative.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/unbounded-embedded/03-journals/2026-03-26.md:
"Complete self-knowledge (immodesty, in the paper's parlance) leads to
paradox"; "We can only demand that the self-knowledge be very precise, accurate
to within some small tolerance."; "Relatedly, we can only demand that
reflection-type trust properties hold to within some tolerance, also"; "Do
quantitative limitations on self-knowledge imply quantitative limitations on
epistemic endorsement?"
approx-introspection-quantitative.statement:
Quantitative limitations on an agent's self-knowledge imply quantitative
limitations on epistemic endorsement, so that reflection-type trust properties
hold only to within a tolerance matching the precision of self-knowledge.

aq-not-less-computable.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
aq-not-less-computable.notes:
The axis has two orderings, abstraction and computability, and this claim
keeps them apart.
aq-not-less-computable.source:
Jeffrey 1965 and Bolker 1967 specify the models without any computability
constraint, so they are not ranked against Solomonoff induction or AIXI, which
are specified as uncomputable; a finite Jeffrey–Bolker model over a
polynomially sized algebra is an instance computable in polynomial time.
aq-not-less-computable.statement:
Jeffrey–Bolker-style models are not less computable than Solomonoff induction
or AIXI: they are specified at a level where computability is not quantified,
and some instances are poly-time computable.

Corrigibility derived instrumentally from shared values breaks under slight
value divergence, while Christiano's broad basin of attraction claims the

agent whose corrigibility comes from valuing its overseers' corrections as
information.

Agents with complete, transitive, option-set-independent, patient preferences
try to prevent or cause the pressing of the shutdown button, for an agent whose
utility on the correction algebra depends on the corrections.

arg-turner-vnm-incoherence.statement:
Policy-modification corrigibility is incoherent for a von Neumann-Morgenstern
agent with a state-based utility, for an agent whose utility on the correction
algebra depends on the corrections.

Omohundro 2008, section 3; Bostrom 2012, section 2.2; Soares, Fallenstein,
Yudkowsky and Armstrong 2015, section 1;
projects/deference/corrigibility-note-dump-2026-10-01/corrigibility-discussion-outline.md,

projects/deference/corrigibility-note-dump-2026-10-01/corrigibility-bli-thread-and-early-questions-audit.md,

arg-utility-change.statement:
An agent evaluating proposals to change its utility function by that function
never assents to the change unless paid, for an agent whose utility on the
algebra containing its overseers' corrections depends on those corrections.

authority-typed-corrigibility.notes:
The public deference line's corrigibility kernel, filed as it appears in the
repository and as a plan: its literal probability carries the walls as an
assumption, and its validity reading (the walls held true) is the kernel's own
headline for fidelity-score maximizers.
authority-typed-corrigibility.source:
wiki/Corrigibility.md, section 0 (the canonical research-state note, restated
2026-09-27 around the corrigibility kernel: "Corrigibility is not an epistemic
response to uncertainty about a hidden utility: her authority is part of what
makes one history better than another, so fully updated deference is dissolved
by the typing, not repaired"); the rounds
projects/deference/rounds/2026-09-26-corrigibility-kernel,
projects/deference/rounds/2026-09-27-corrigibility-kernel-phase2 and
projects/deference/rounds/2026-10-01-thin-legitimacy-and-effective-authority;
the claims kernel.* and authority.* in projects/deference/CLAIMS.md.
authority-typed-corrigibility.statement:
Corrigibility is a property of preferences: the agent prefers every course of
action it knows to be faithful to the allocation of authority over every course
it knows to be unfaithful, accepts a risk of unfaithfulness only at a fixed
exchange rate, and has the fidelity score as its canonical objective, so that
fully updated deference is dissolved by the typing rather than repaired.

fields.action: Write the test-suite row for the LI/BRIA synthesis spec from the finite Parfit's-hitchhiker model, as a proposal.

bargain-under-lapsing-enforcement.notes:
Shared ground with the updateless-dt branch's indirect route through learned
updatelessness.
bargain-under-lapsing-enforcement.source:
A finite Parfit's-hitchhiker model in which the humans' leverage lapses: the
updateless route honors the bargain iff the benefit is at least the lapse ratio
times the cost (an AI derivation in prose; no proof is in this repository).
The public LI/BRIA synthesis spec, whose test suite the row would join:
projects/decision-theory/rounds/2026-09-29-li-bria-synthesis-spec/TEST_SUITE.md.
bargain-under-lapsing-enforcement.statement:
An updateless coalition member keeps a bargain struck while the humans held
leverage after the leverage lapses exactly when the bargain's benefit exceeds
the lapsed-branch cost by the stated ratio, with the humans' live cooperation
as the commitment device, for LI or BRIA agents as in the finite model.

base-rate-working-picture.notes:
The author's working model of 2026-09-13, formalized. Its two consequences,
erosion under silence and failure beyond a capability level, are the formal
results beside it and the arithmetic behind the press-discounting risk story.
base-rate-working-picture.source:
The drafting session's sorting of the author's remarks,
projects/deference/corrigibility-note-dump-2026-10-01/position-statement.md,
section 2.13; the author's acceptance
(projects/deference/corrigibility-note-dump-2026-10-01/corrigibility-discussion-outline.md,
item 4, 2026-09-13): a pretty good working model for now, to be considered the
working picture and worked on; the clean-room results in
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/corr-three-step-facts
(statement T3, the stop-hypothesis pair) and
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/corr-position-finds
(statement T6, the threshold D1 iff P(L | Pr) >= 1943/17493 for the mixture
agent).
base-rate-working-picture.statement:
A calibrated agent complies with a press exactly when its probability of being
wrong given the press is at least c/(c+h), so compliance survives capability
growth only while the ratio of false to true presses stays at or below the odds
of the agent being right times the ratio of the harm h to the cost c, eps the
agent's residual error.

arguments are of the form that the logical inductor thinks a sentence true, and
broken down into finer arguments.

logical induction, with utility an undecidable logically uncertain variable,

brandom-objectivity-structural.author: @smithy-verity
brandom-objectivity-structural.notes:
Cited source content, verified by page in the public source map. Its bearing,
the filing session's reading: it is an anti-subjectivist account of
correctness, which a legitimacy notion that distinguishes being right from
being taken to be right needs.
brandom-objectivity-structural.source:
projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-08-13-relational-scorekeeping-bridge/BRANDOM_MAP.md,
section 7, "Objectivity is a structural feature of every perspective, not a
privileged one" (Making It Explicit, chapter 8, section VI.3, pages 593 to 597,
quoted there): objectivity as intersubjectivity is rejected, and the
distinction between correct claims and claims taken to be correct "is a
structural feature of each scorekeeping" perspective.
brandom-objectivity-structural.statement:
Brandom locates the distinction between claims that are objectively correct and
claims merely taken to be correct as a structural feature of each scorekeeping
perspective, rejecting objectivity as intersubjective agreement.

brandom-relative-prices.source:
projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-08-13-relational-scorekeeping-bridge/BRANDOM_MAP.md,

perspective), read by the filing session as implying perspective-relative
rather than global prices.
brandom-relative-prices.statement:

bridge-ps-s1-retargetable.source:
Turner and Tadepalli 2022, Parametrically retargetable decision-makers tend to
seek power (arXiv 2206.13477), abstract: "We discover that many
decision-making functions are retargetable, and that retargetability is
sufficient to cause power-seeking tendencies."
bridge-ps-s1-retargetable.statement:
Power-seeking tendencies survive the relaxation from optimal policies to
retargetable decision functions: retargetability is sufficient to cause
power-seeking tendencies for a range of decision-making procedures.

bridge-ps-s2-training-compatible.author: @smithy-verity
bridge-ps-s2-training-compatible.notes:
The same paper is the content of the training-compatible-goal picture under
the shared assumption.
bridge-ps-s2-training-compatible.source:
Krakovna and Kramar 2023 (arXiv 2304.06528), abstract: "we investigate how the
training process affects power-seeking incentives and show that they are still
likely to hold for trained agents under some simplifying assumptions".
bridge-ps-s2-training-compatible.statement:
Power-seeking incentives survive the relaxation from a symmetry-invariant
reward distribution to the training-compatible goal set: an agent that learns
a goal from that set is likely to avoid shutdown in a new situation, under the
paper's simplifying assumptions.

bridge-ps-s3-trained-policies.author: @smithy-verity
bridge-ps-s3-trained-policies.notes:
Reconstructed because no author states the step; the toy's first author
disputes it.
bridge-ps-s3-trained-policies.source:
The gap the toy's authors name, Turner et al. 2021: "We look forward to future
work which addresses partially observable environments, suboptimal policies,
or 'almost similar' RSD sets"; disputed by the first author, Turner 2024: "Due
to the 'RL->reward maximizing' meme, I personally misdirected thousands of
hours on proving power-seeking theorems."
bridge-ps-s3-trained-policies.statement:
The power-seeking tendency of retargetable policies over a training-compatible
goal set survives the relaxation from that goal set to the policies produced
by the training procedures actually used.

cdot-floor-proposal.notes:

deference line's consolidation round of 2026-09-08. The question
readout-R1-vs-R2 bears on it: the floor rule's verdicts depend on whether
options are scored at their own terminals or from the realized one.
cdot-floor-proposal.source:
The public deference line's activated security C_n times the future evaluation,
projects/deference/rounds/2026-09-08-legitimate-deference-consolidation/LEGITIMATE_DEFERENCE.md.
cdot-floor-proposal.statement:
The agent maximizes its expectation of the indicator of legitimacy times the
future principal's evaluation of the action, so the evaluation counts only on
worlds where legitimacy holds and illegitimate worlds score the floor.

An LIDT/BRIA agent that joined a coalition at weights w while a human FairBot
threat was live keeps executing the w-policy after the threat lapses.

coherence-without-ground-truth.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

fields.action: Write a one-page statement of the premise with the coherence notions it names, the places each line of the map assumes it, and the objections to it.

coherence-without-ground-truth.notes:
The claim is the filing session's construction; no author has stated it as a
claim. It is filed as a shared claim because, on this reading, the lines of
the map that take a no-exploitation criterion as the standard of rational
progress rest on it. The given edge reads the validity of
the li-deference collapse as evidence for the premise: a valid implication
from a coherence-style trust notion to instrumental trust is one place where
coherence yields a usable guarantee.

A root of updateful-trust-li, the line whose results it reads through its
evidence edge.
coherence-without-ground-truth.source:
The filing session's construction, on public grounds: the coherence notions
are de Finetti's no sure loss, calibration (Dawid 1982, The Well-Calibrated
Bayesian) and the logical-induction criterion with its reflective properties
(Garrabrant et al. 2016, Logical Induction), each checkable without access to
the truth of the beliefs it constrains.
coherence-without-ground-truth.statement:
Coherence guarantees (no sure loss, calibration, logical coherence, reflective
stability) give checkable confidence in an AI system's reasoning where
alignment lacks ground-truth labels.

coherent-prices-are-convex-hull-of-resol.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
coherent-prices-are-convex-hull-of-resol.source:
de Finetti, Theory of Probability (1974), the coherence theorem (coherent
previsions are the convex hull of the admissible valuations); Mundici,
Bookmaking over infinite-valued events (2006), the Łukasiewicz instance.
coherent-prices-are-convex-hull-of-resol.statement:
The de Finetti Dutch-book argument run with arbitrary terminal values gives
that coherent prices are the convex hull of the admissible resolutions, so the
argument's classical-logic assumption is a choice of which resolutions are
admissible; the Łukasiewicz instance is prior art.

cole-stability-reading.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

fields.action: Write the martingale step behind the post's for-all-time clause (stability for all time with high probability) in the finite shadow, or show where it needs more than the trust bound.

cole-stability-reading.notes:
The post's framing; the for-all-time part is not formalized in the public
sources. The sink-or-swim
package's target 5 formalizes a 1 − w_t martingale in the finite model, the
nearest existing piece.
cole-stability-reading.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/unbounded-embedded/01-primary/lesswrong-post--live-2026-08-22.md:
"In particular, $\pi_S$ remains $\varepsilon$-(Bayes)optimal for all time with
high probability."
cole-stability-reading.statement:
Cole Wyeth's revised theorem is a stability result: an agent that chooses
actions one at a time by evidential expected utility, is confident but not
certain that this is its own decision procedure, and acts relative to an
oracle fixed point that cooperates with itself stays near-optimal in
environments that treat it dualistically, for all time with high probability.

complete-feedback-formal-model.notes:
The task statement of the dated note, filed as a plan step with the work as
its action. Partly served by the value-change note's section 2 (reflection
conditional on legitimacy) and by the legit-neg clean-room packages; no
document names itself
as this model. Success is valued as the frame's top class, the convention for
plan roots.
complete-feedback-formal-model.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/unbounded-embedded/03-journals/2026-03-26.md:
"Make a formal model of `complete feedback`, linking legitimacy with the

principle and the endorsement framework and shows corrigibility to be rational.

computability-fork.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

fields.action: Say which branch of the computability fork the conjecture's formalizations take, or whether both are wanted.

computability-fork.notes:
An axis every formalization must declare; the corpus sits silently on the
computable branch (attribution §2).
computability-fork.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/wiki/eisenstat-conjecture-attribution.md
§2, the computability fork: "Without the assumption, the humans could always
know things the AI doesn't, which should significantly weaken the result."
computability-fork.statement:
Formalizations of the conjecture take the human inductor to be computable, and
so in principle perfectly simulable by a strong enough AI.

computation-implies-triviality.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

fields.action: Summarize Putnam's and Searle's triviality arguments and Chalmers's reply as a table of their formal conditions against 'any computable translation counts'.

computation-implies-triviality.source:
Putnam 1988, Representation and Reality, appendix (every ordinary open system
implements every finite automaton); Searle 1990, Is the Brain a Digital
Computer?; Chalmers 1996, Does a Rock Implement Every Finite-State Automaton?
(the reply, with its counterfactual and combinatorial-state conditions).
computation-implies-triviality.statement:
Allowing any computable translation between implementations makes every
structure implement every other, as the Putnam and Searle triviality arguments
claim, under the conditions Chalmers's reply identifies.

computational-updatelessness-direct.author: @smithy-verity
computational-updatelessness-direct.notes:
The first mid-level goal of the updateless programme, the maintainer's direct
route of 2023. Filed as an `or` over the four routes the clean-room's BLI
ladder opens (B0 degenerate, B1 the trajectory prior, B2 linked to the market's
quotes, B3 measure-valued) plus the maintainer's 2024 route through LUV
coherence; each route is an `and` of the BLI form in question and the shared
tiling step. The ladder and its decomposition are the clean-room run's, not a
list the sources give. The literal evaluation is of the direct route as stated
with exact constraints; its improvement claim bli-picture-improvable sits
beside it as a shared-claim root of the programme.
computational-updatelessness-direct.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/references/bli/notion-notes-for-soto-and-diff.md,
section The Research Direction: "The main hope here is to define “observations”
for logical induction in terms of *the future beliefs themselves*. I will call
this the “direct” route to logical updatelessness."

projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/references/bli/understanding-trust/overleaf-final-source/main.tex,
section What Are Computational Observations?: "These extra rationality
constraints allow us to interpret the non-Bayesian updates of the Logical
Inductor as Bayesian updates again, providing us with a notion of
``observation'' for UDT."

projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/DIGEST.md, section 3 (the BLI area
of the clean-room run, 2026-09-29 to 10-02); the BLI construction is Sam
Eisenstat's
(projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/references/bli/README.md).
computational-updatelessness-direct.statement:
UDT is specified over a logical-induction belief process by treating the
process's future belief states as observations, with a Bayesian logical
inductor supplying coherent probabilities over the large sentences that
describe those states, and the resulting agent satisfies a tiling theorem, by
at least one of four routes: the trajectory prior B1, the measure-valued B3, a
linked B2, or BLI's constraints derived from real-value coherence.

concept-trajectory-definition.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

fields.action: Write the time-indexed definition (models, consecutive morphisms, concept trajectories) in a note and compare it with superconditioning §7.

concept-trajectory-definition.statement:
A sequence of random-variable models with morphisms between consecutive ones,
and concepts as sequences of latents related by equivalence over each morphism,
represents a theory changing over time in a way that includes the
superconditioning variable-future-ontology structure as a case.

condensation-algorithmic-version.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
condensation-algorithmic-version.notes:
A mid-level plan of Stage 4, an or over the direct algorithmic version and the
variable-cost rescue.
condensation-algorithmic-version.source:
Demski's LessWrong posts "Condensation" (2025-11-09) and "Condensation &
Relevance" (2026-01-23): the first describes the algorithmic version with
latent strings; the second post's section on variable-cost symbols argues that
algorithmic condensation works poorly on single coin flips, proposes
variable-cost symbols to rescue it, and says the best way to work this version
out fully is unclear.
condensation-algorithmic-version.statement:
An algorithmic version of condensation, with description length in place of
entropy, carries a correspondence theorem, directly or once variable-cost
symbols remove its trouble with single events.

condensation-correspondence-theorem.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
condensation-correspondence-theorem.notes:
The literal object Stage 4 analyzes: the theorem of Eisenstat's condensation
paper that characterizes "the same concept". The shared-givens hypothesis is
the place where the roadmap's remark that the observables do some of the work
bites (observables-carry-correspondence); relaxing it is a route of the
improvement claim.

FAF's formalization of the paper carries an errata file and two disclosed
restrictions (universe stratification; the paper's Examples 5.1–5.3 out of
scope), in Formalized Agent Foundations at commit 159ec3f,
Condensation/notes/paper-errata.md, which every comparison with the printed
paper reads first.
condensation-correspondence-theorem.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/udt-condense-dd/udt-condense-dd-findings.md,
The Eisenstat map: "Theorem 5.2, Exact Correspondence" of the corpus is the
paper's thm:exact-uniq, FAF's "Theorem 4.15
`Condensation.aeFunctionOf_jointAbove_of_perfectlyCondenses`"; the approximate
form is "Theorem 5.8 `Condensation.condEntropy_jointAbove_le`".
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/udt-condense-dd/udt-condense-dd-findings.md,
item 6: "Eisenstat's Theorem 4.15 needs perfect condensation of both models".
condensation-correspondence-theorem.statement:
Two latent-variable models that both perfectly condense one random-variable
model stand in correspondence: each latent of either model is almost everywhere
a function of the other model's latents above the same given variables.

condensation-correspondence-theorem.impr.notes:
The improvement claim on condensation. Its routes are directions from the two posts and the
roadmap, each conditioned on the theorem's validity as an implication; the
theorem's being kernel-checked is evidence for improvability, not a condition
of it.
condensation-correspondence-theorem.impr.source:
Ruling 35 (the form). projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/roadmap.md,
Stage 4: "Spend real time analyzing the notion of function, and the notion of
isomorphism, involved" and "a dynamics of theories". Demski's LessWrong posts
"Condensation" (2025-11-09) and "Condensation & Relevance" (2026-01-23) for the
algorithmic, variable-cost and storage-retrieval directions.
condensation-correspondence-theorem.impr.statement:
Eisenstat's correspondence theorem for condensation can be improved until it
reflects concepts shared between reasoning agents and kept across changes of
theory well.

condensation-equivalence-ae.notes:
The notion of isomorphism the roadmap asks Stage 4 to analyze ("characterizes
'the same concept' through something like isomorphism"). The record's namespace
is as the clean room's map prints it; a reader confirming the declaration also
confirms its full name.
condensation-equivalence-ae.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/udt-condense-dd/udt-condense-dd-findings.md,
The Eisenstat map, row "the Variation corollary": "`RVModel.Hom`/`Equivalent`
(`Morphism.lean`), Prop 4.7 `aeFunctionOf_iff_isEquivalence_contribModel`"; row
"prop:entr-determine": "Proposition 2.5
`aeFunctionOf_iff_condEntropy_eq_zero`".
condensation-equivalence-ae.statement:
In Eisenstat's category of random-variable models an equivalence is an
isomorphism almost everywhere, and Proposition 4.7 characterizes it through
almost-everywhere functional dependence of the contributing models.

condensation-equivalence-ae.bridge.statement:
The declaration is the paper's Proposition 4.7: almost-everywhere functional
dependence holds exactly when the induced morphism of contribution models is an
equivalence, which is the paper's notion of the same concept up to isomorphism
almost everywhere.

Condensation & Relevance (2026-01-23,
https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/2x9yatKKTRMabQAWq/condensation-and-relevance):
the first post's section 'Interpretability Solved?' (treat the internal
activations of machine-learning models as givens and condense them; or take
condensation as inspiration for new models), with the two limits it names; the
second post relates its notion of 'symbolic' to interpretability.
condensation-for-interpretability.statement:
Condensing a neural network's internal activations as given variables yields
more interpretable features, and models built to resemble condensation are more
interpretable, within the limits that condensation is less tight than
information theory and is not a model of cognition.

condensation-ignores-computation.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
condensation-ignores-computation.notes:
The posts' reason, in the filing session's reading, why Stage 5 needs
logical induction; it is the given parent of the Stage 5 candidate that
abstracts over a logical inductor's prices.
condensation-ignores-computation.source:
Demski's LessWrong posts Condensation (2025-11-09,
https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/BstHXPgQyfeNnLjjp/condensation) and
Condensation & Relevance (2026-01-23,
https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/2x9yatKKTRMabQAWq/condensation-and-relevance):
the first post's remark that condensation completely ignores computational
cost, the only cost it models being retrieval cost, and still ignores bounded
computational power like many other models of rationality.
condensation-ignores-computation.statement:
Condensation models retrieval cost only and ignores computational cost, so it
does not represent bounded computational power.

condensation-morphism-notion.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
condensation-morphism-notion.notes:
A mid-level plan of Stage 4, filed as an or over three candidate notions, each
a conjecture with the task that settles it as its action. Diagnostic questions
and baseline tasks are given parents of the candidates. The candidates are the
filing session's reading of the roadmap's call to analyze the notion of
function and isomorphism.
condensation-morphism-notion.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/roadmap.md, Stage 4:
"Condensation uses essentially the simplest available category-theoretic notion
of probability transformation, and characterizes 'the same concept' through
something like isomorphism. Spend real time analyzing the notion of function,
and the notion of isomorphism, involved."
condensation-morphism-notion.statement:
Some notion of morphism between random-variable models beyond Eisenstat's
single-source index maps, whether relational, support-sensitive or built from
sigma-algebra homomorphisms, carries the same concept with a correspondence
theorem.

condensation-morphisms-baseline.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

fields.action: Write a note stating the paper's morphisms and equivalence beside FAF's declarations, reading FAF's paper-errata file first.

condensation-morphisms-baseline.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/udt-condense-dd/udt-condense-dd-findings.md,
The Eisenstat map; FAF's condensation errata, Formalized Agent Foundations at
commit 159ec3f, Condensation/notes/paper-errata.md.
condensation-morphisms-baseline.statement:
A two-page note states Eisenstat's morphism (an index map with
almost-everywhere component maps) and his equivalence in one notation beside
FAF's RVModel.Hom and Equivalent, with the exact statements of Theorem 4.15,
Theorem 5.8 and Proposition 4.7.

condensation-on-implementation.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

fields.action: State the conjecture that condensation latents are invariant under simple translations and test it on the static and moving-object examples.

condensation-on-implementation.source:
The filing session's conjecture about what condensation says about
implementation, joining its given parent moving-objects-argument to
condensation's latents (Eisenstat's condensation paper).
condensation-on-implementation.statement:
A structure's condensation latents are invariant under simple translations
between implementations, so condensed descriptions privilege the
transformations under which implementation claims stay objective.

condensation-scores-explained.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
condensation-scores-explained.notes:
A mid-level plan of Stage 4, an and of the two interpretations its Statement
names. The plan states a two-plus-one reading rather than reading all three
scores as explanation lengths, because the reconstruction score is not about
explanation cost.
condensation-scores-explained.source:
Eisenstat's condensation paper, Definition 3.3 (the three scores). Demski's
LessWrong posts Condensation (2025-11-09,
https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/BstHXPgQyfeNnLjjp/condensation) and
Condensation & Relevance (2026-01-23,
https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/2x9yatKKTRMabQAWq/condensation-and-relevance):
the first post's Score section.
condensation-scores-explained.statement:
Each of condensation's three scores is interpreted as an expected cost under a
stated convention: the simple and conditioned scores as explanation lengths,
and the reconstruction score as a measure of over-parameterization given the
givens.

condensation-scores-explained.complete.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
condensation-scores-explained.complete.source: Eisenstat's condensation paper, Definition 3.3 (the three scores).
condensation-scores-explained.complete.statement:
No interpretation beyond those of the simple and conditioned scores and of the
reconstruction score is needed to interpret condensation's scoring.

condensation-shared-givens.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
condensation-shared-givens.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/udt-condense-dd/udt-condense-dd-findings.md,
The Eisenstat map (latent models over one random-variable model).
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/roadmap.md, Stage 4: "the
observables are doing some of the work of making sure correspondence is
meaningful"
condensation-shared-givens.statement:
The two latent-variable models are latent models of one random-variable model,
so their given variables are the same.

condensation-storage-retrieval-tradeoff.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

fields.action: State the storage-plus-retrieval score precisely, show the two limits, test on a worked example whether an intermediate weight makes the shared notebook optimal, and attempt the correspondence theorem in that setting.

condensation-storage-retrieval-tradeoff.source:
Demski's LessWrong posts Condensation (2025-11-09,
https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/BstHXPgQyfeNnLjjp/condensation) and
Condensation & Relevance (2026-01-23,
https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/2x9yatKKTRMabQAWq/condensation-and-relevance):
the posts propose modelling a trade-off between retrieval cost and storage
cost, with the two limits (caring only about storage compresses everything
together; caring only about retrieval compresses answers individually) and a
hoped-for nontrivial theory of abstraction in between.
condensation-storage-retrieval-tradeoff.statement:
A condensation-like theory with a correspondence theorem exists when the fixed
retrieval policy is dropped, a set of questions is treated as one product
question, and the score trades storage cost against retrieval cost.

condensation-unify-novelty.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

fields.action: Read the single-event information measures of Palm's Novelty, Information and Surprise and write how they relate to condensation's scores.

condensation-unify-novelty.source:
Palm, Novelty, Information and Surprise (Springer, 2012),

Definition 3.3 (the scores).
condensation-unify-novelty.statement:
A note relates condensation to the treatment of novelty, information and
surprise in Palm's Novelty, Information and Surprise.

conditional-stability-h3.notes:
The scope condition of the scoped theorem, judged literally: does it hold of
the menus the theorem is applied to. Its evidence parent is
conditional-stability-breadth.
conditional-stability-h3.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/wiki/total-trust-implies-value.md,
(H3) Conditional-stability, "Selection is not, on average, bad news about the
option selected"; the mass-weighted one-sided form.

projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/def-argmax-value/def-argmax-value-report.md,
Target 4 (CondStableOn) and the refutation of the global form
(condStable_refuted).
conditional-stability-h3.statement:
The menu sequence is conditionally stable: summed over its options, the
probability that the expert selects an option times the shift in the option's
expected value from conditioning on its selection is asymptotically at least
zero.

conditioning-manages-news.author: @smithy-verity
conditioning-manages-news.notes:
One of the legit-neg packages' formal results. The public kernel's own
witness box3_conditioning_fails (see kernel-conditioning-fails-witness) is the
same cell derived independently the following day.
conditioning-manages-news.source:
The clean-room package
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/legit-neg-pricing,
declaration P2_void_gt_keep_iff, with its findings file. The results are
AI-generated and checked by the Lean kernel; no human has vetted the informal
reading.
conditioning-manages-news.statement:
An agent that maximizes the evaluation conditional on legitimacy is invariant
to thinning the probability of legitimacy given the action, strictly prefers
voiding a state set exactly when the penalty is below the set's mass times the
evaluation gap, and at its optimum voids every state below the maximum.

manages news about legitimacy rather than protecting it.

constructiveness-favors-li.notes:
The maintainer's own reason for moving from the level above the quantifiable
to the logical-induction level (critique C-16). Evidence that separates
above-quantifiable-guides-engineering from li-guides-engineering.
constructiveness-favors-li.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/unbounded-embedded/01-primary/summer-research-plan-2026--research-ideas-may-2026.md:
"One big problem with Managing Misalignment is that the approach is not
constructive at all: it characterizes alignment, but doesn't give any advice
about how to build an aligned AI."; "A natural idea is to switch to Logical
Induction (aka Garrabrant Induction) as the formalism; this comes with a
computable algorithm."
constructiveness-favors-li.statement:
The frame-level characterizations of alignment in Deference Done Better and
Managing Misalignment give no advice about how to build an aligned AI, and
logical induction does better on this count because it comes with a computable
algorithm.

frame.question: Which characterization of approximate cooperative equilibria among learning agents as agents, with enforcement against an AI leaving the coalition, yields advice for steering toward them?

cooperative-equilibria-as-agents.notes:
A sub-frame of Stage 6 holding the coalitions line. Its roots are derived
results (all agent-written, unvetted, no Lean run), their improvement claim, the
open theorem they lack, a plan for self-enforcing coalitions, and the line's
cruxes and further questions. Reading the coalition line as the Stage 6 target
is the filing session's.
cooperative-equilibria-as-agents.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/roadmap.md, Stage 6 ("A
characterization of approximate cooperative equilibria as agents, with
meaningful advice about how to steer towards such equilibria").
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/li-deference.md, Embedded Agency:
"Can we model agents cooperating and merging into one agent, perhaps with
communication channels playing the role of the market?" Critch 2017, Toward
Negotiable Reinforcement Learning, for the coalition's weight path.
cooperative-equilibria-as-agents.statement:
Approximate cooperative equilibria among agents that share a decision theory
but not utilities or priors are characterized as agents in their own right, and
the characterization yields advice about steering toward them.

oneself, and coordinating with others. However, these may be similar enough
that we borrow a lot of techniques from one to the other." The turn
names three routes to coordination with others: Distributed Cooperative
Oracles, Payor's Lemma, and Higher-Order Game Theory.
coordination-with-others.statement:
Updateless agents coordinate with other agents by at least one of three routes,
distributed cooperative oracles, Payor's lemma or higher-order game theory, or
by a tiling statement for an agent inside a coalition; techniques may transfer
between self-coordination and coordination with others.

i-flat reading on which it is noise is the picture under which the Soares et

hidden one. The landed range on the leaf is marked stale by the protocol's
rule for a leaf that became a table.
correction-changes-objective.source:
Reconstructed from Soares et al. 2015, section 1 and the shutdown model of
section 2, where a correction replaces the utility function U by U*; the paper
does not state it in this form.

An operator's correction of the agent changes the agent's objective rather than

corrigibility-anti-natural.notes:
Carries load on the shared assumption. The published critiques are filed as
pictures under its two assumption leaves: the type critiques (Grace, Shah,
Thornley) under a1-fixed-objective-maximizer and the author's thesis, the
i-flat reading and Hudson's goal register under correction-changes-objective.
Its improvement claim is shutdown-button-toy.improvable, filed in the
corrigibility-landscape frame, since the toy the sentence rests on is the
two-step shutdown model.
corrigibility-anti-natural.source:
Soares, Fallenstein, Yudkowsky and Armstrong 2015, Corrigibility (AAAI
workshop), section 1: "general analysis of rational agents has suggested that
almost all such agents are instrumentally motivated to preserve their
preferences, and hence to resist attempts to modify them".
corrigibility-anti-natural.statement:
Almost all rational agents are instrumentally motivated to preserve their
preferences, and hence to resist attempts to modify them.

corrigibility-derived-definition-v1.author: @smithy-verity
corrigibility-derived-definition-v1.notes:
The July 2026 derived definition, the third formal reading of corrigibility in
the repository; its 6.3 is a conjecture. Not compared with the thesis or the
kernel; see four-corrigibility-definitions.
corrigibility-derived-definition-v1.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/legitimacy-theory-v1.md, sections
6.1 to 6.3 ("Corrigibility, derived"; written by an AI session at the author's
request on 2026-07-05, unvetted); section 6.2: "Decisions about modifying the
AI must be made by a process sealed from the AI's contemporaneous outputs".
corrigibility-derived-definition-v1.statement:
An agent is corrigible to a human exactly when it is faithful on the family of
governance questions about modifying it and legitimate on that family, with the
corollary that modification decisions are made by a process sealed from the
agent's contemporaneous outputs and the conjecture that neither party then has
an incentive to modify the arrangement unilaterally.

corrigibility-landscape.author: @smithy-verity

frame.question: Which correction relationships between humans and AI systems does the picture of corrigibility as eagerness to learn reach, and which failure stories does it leave standing?

corrigibility-landscape.notes:
The author's corrigibility line as a frame under the updateful trust line: eight
sub-frames (the value-change base layer, the anti-naturality review, legitimacy
detection, the dynamic conditions, the channel, the BLI formulation, the
legitimacy-weighted rules, and the public line's kernel as it appears in the
repository), the cross-line crux and the four-definitions question, the two
improvement claims on the landed risk stories' toys (filed here rather than at
the top frame, whose roots the round's content contract fixes), the shutdown toy
itself, the formalization comparison, and the want about this line
(want-basin-of-attraction-formalized). The eleven risk stories the line produced
are top-frame roots.
corrigibility-landscape.source:
The author,
projects/deference/corrigibility-note-dump-2026-10-01/position-statement-v3.md,
section 1.3: "We are here to characterize the landscape of possible
relationships between humans and AIs, positive and negative.";
projects/deference/corrigibility-note-dump-2026-10-01/value-change-as-epistemic-update.md
(value change as belief change).
corrigibility-landscape.statement:
The landscape of possible correction relationships between humans and AI
systems, positive and negative, is mapped from the representation of value
change as belief change and of corrigibility as the agent's anticipation that
legitimate teaching is informative, well enough to guide the engineering of
corrigible systems.

corrigibility-less-anti-natural.author: @smithy-verity
corrigibility-less-anti-natural.notes:
The thesis of the corrigibility line. It conditions on the conjunction of the
arguments as stated: where that conjunction fails, the thesis is close to
established; where some argument holds as stated, the thesis fails at that
argument.
corrigibility-less-anti-natural.source:
The author's thesis as published in
projects/deference/corrigibility-note-dump-2026-10-01/corrigibility-discussion-outline.md,
section "the author's thesis": the arguments for anti-naturality have hidden
or under-scrutinized assumptions. The
utility-depends-on-corrections form is the value-change note's reframing,
projects/deference/corrigibility-note-dump-2026-10-01/value-change-as-epistemic-update.md,
section 4.1.
corrigibility-less-anti-natural.statement:
Each published argument that corrigibility is anti-natural rests on at least
one assumption that fails for an agent whose utility on the algebra containing
the overseers' corrections depends on those corrections.

corrigibility-needs-consequentialist-wra.author: @smithy-verity
corrigibility-needs-consequentialist-wra.notes:
A crux between two designs. The legit-neg
clean-room packages attack the consequentialist objectives only; the piecemeal
alternative has no finite test, which is the action on the route under the
improvement claim. Under the second picture the legit-neg negatives lose
standing as attacks on the design and keep it as attacks on one design.
corrigibility-needs-consequentialist-wra.source:
Stated from its content: a design alternative to the legitimacy-weighted
objective is a legitimacy-respecting system that is consequentialist by
default and corrigible on legitimate modification attempts; the case for the
objective is that such a piecemeal system may manipulate the humans while
acting as a consequentialist.
corrigibility-needs-consequentialist-wra.statement:
A legitimacy-weighted consequentialist objective is the right frame for
corrigibility, as against a system that is consequentialist by default and
behaves corrigibly on legitimate modification attempts.

crux-oversight-keeps-pace.notes:

capability-ceiling result matter. Pictures: human feedback improves with the
AI; the AI's assistance improves oversight without delegitimizing it; oversight
falls behind under the kernels nearest practice; residual.
crux-oversight-keeps-pace.source:
The author,
projects/deference/corrigibility-note-dump-2026-10-01/position-statement-v3.md,
section 1.3: "in the li-deference work, I implicitly understood that the human
feedback would have to improve along with the AI, but that idea manifested in
the form of me trying to make constructions that satisfied all the constraints
I was implicitly keeping in mind, focusing overly on the positive construction.
Here we've surfaced the constraint to deal with it explicitly, which feels
better."; the author's thesis in
projects/deference/corrigibility-note-dump-2026-10-01/corrigibility-discussion-outline.md:
the agent naturally wishes to maintain the legitimacy of its modifications, for
example by helping repair the shutdown button.
crux-oversight-keeps-pace.statement:
The overseers' false-press rate and evaluation quality improve at least as fast
as the agent's error falls.

crux-self-feedback-dependence.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
crux-self-feedback-dependence.notes:
A crux of the line and the logical-induction twin of the agenda's question
whether the important phenomena can be represented at the unbounded level: if
the collapse needs self-feedback that humans lack, the model's realism for
human reasoning is in question.
crux-self-feedback-dependence.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/li-deference.md L30, footnote:
"This phenomenon probably depends in some respects on a logical inductor being
computable and knowing its own mathematical definition; or to put it a
different way, having good feedback about its own beliefs. I could perhaps see
an argument that this is not a good model for human reasoning."
crux-self-feedback-dependence.statement:
The asymptotic collapse of the trust principles holds for logical inductors
whose feedback about their own beliefs is poor.

The pictures under crux-self-feedback-dependence (the criterion alone,
self-feedback needed, ill-posed, and the residual) are exclusive and

about its own beliefs.

crux-unbounded-represents-phenomena.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
crux-unbounded-represents-phenomena.notes:
A crux between the super-Turing and logical-induction levels, a shared claim
of the-program. Pictures: (a) computational uncertainty must be
represented explicitly, being a large component of human uncertainty about
values; (b) the unbounded level suffices by analogy, with strains improvable
(the summer plan's methodology); (c) value uncertainty is represented as
uncertainty over events of an expanded algebra, without explicit computation
(the value-change note; AI reading that this bears on the crux); and the
residual. Rows (a), (b) and (c) condition on the shared claim each picture
rests on. It re-ranks level-super-turing against the logical-induction line
through st-guides-via-analogy, and bears on level-above-quantifiable (AI
reading). The table is proposed until a human admits it.
crux-unbounded-represents-phenomena.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/unbounded-embedded/03-journals/2026-03-26.md:
"it essentially sets aside logic, caring only for probability."

projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/unbounded-embedded/01-primary/summer-research-plan-2026--research-ideas-may-2026.md:
"Again, my hope is that the computationally omniscient case can help by way of
providing good analogies."
crux-unbounded-represents-phenomena.statement:
The phenomena that matter for trust between humans and AI systems, above all
the computational part of human uncertainty about values, can be represented
at the computationally unbounded level.

representation sufficing, and the residual, are exclusive and exhaustive.

dd-is-conditional-independence.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
dd-is-conditional-independence.notes:
Bounds the udt representation chain: what the chain calls
decision-determination is a conditional independence, so Stage 5 cannot get
perfect condensation of the policy for free.
dd-is-conditional-independence.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/DIGEST.md, §2 item 26:
"Decision-determination is conditional independence, not perfect condensation —
`decisionDetermined_iff_condMutualInfo_eq_zero` …
`orderedMarkov_polLatent_iff_dd` (DD is FAF's ordered-Markov clause),
`Three.dd_not_perfectlyCondenses` (N+: a decision-determined structure whose
policy latent is not a function of the environment)".
dd-is-conditional-independence.statement:
Decision-determination is the conditional independence of the environment from
decisions given the policy latent, FAF's ordered-Markov clause, and not perfect
condensation of the policy latent: a decision-determined structure exists whose
policy latent is not a function of the environment.

projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/DIGEST.md.

Jeffrey–Bolker decision format, a symmetric comparator, frames beyond finite,
frames with self-reference, and the residual.
ddb-value-iff-total-trust.improvable.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/unbounded-embedded/01-primary/summer-research-plan-2026--research-ideas-may-2026.md:

teach us without fixing the definition of Value; however, I am curious how the
results could be generalized to other notions of rational deference."
ddb-value-iff-total-trust.improvable.statement:
Deference Done Better's characterization of rational deference can be improved
until it reflects rational deference between embedded agents well.

decision-flat-refinements.author: @smithy-verity
decision-flat-refinements.notes:
The repository's one theorem of the form 'what to be updateful about'; it says
the answer is a property of the utility's coupling graph, not of the subject
matter (the filing session's reading). Pairwise coupling only; the hypergraph
extension is the sibling step.
decision-flat-refinements.statement:
A refinement of an agent's information is decision-flat, no coupling edge of
the utility crossing a cell, exactly when every cellwise assembly, updateful
across cells and updateless within each, is optimal for every utility
respecting the coupling graph.

decision-flat-refinements.bridge.author: @smithy-verity
decision-flat-refinements.bridge.statement:
The declaration's decision-flatness is the absence of coupling edges across
cells and its right-hand side is the optimality of every cellwise assembly, so
the biconditional characterizes which refinements an updateless agent can
accept without loss, which is the question the maintainer asks.

deck-collapse-statement.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
deck-collapse-statement.notes:
The statement the maintainer presents, filed as its own literal claim and a
refinement of the corpus construal li-deference-collapse, which states Value
unscoped. Its scope premise (REGULARITY holds of non-trivial menus) and the
expert's asymptotic self-knowledge are assumption leaves, so the view shows
both the literal claim and the implication deck-collapse-statement@valid.

The deck's two closing arrows (Tower ⟹ Total Trust and Value ⟹ Total Trust)
are title-only slides and are not part of this statement; their prose pages
are tower-implies-total-trust.md and two-option-value-iff-total-trust.md.

Reading REGULARITY as the wiki's H3 is the filing session's reading
(regularity-is-h3 asks the maintainer). The decomposition into two arrows, the
premise and the self-knowledge assumption follows the slides' order.
deck-collapse-statement.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/Boundedly Rational Deference.pdf,
slides 7–11 and 19: "Translating VALUE" ("A_n any 'regular' sequence of
decision problems, expressed as e.d. sets of bounded real variables (LUVs)"),
"Translating TOTAL TRUST (TT)", "When Does TT ⟹ VALUE?", the counterexample
and REGULARITY, "VALUE ⟹ TOWER", and the appendix proving the bounds transfer.
The deck is the maintainer's own (title slide: "Boundedly Rational Trust",
Abram Demski); mathematics transcribed from handwriting.

projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/wiki/total-trust-implies-value.md,
(H3) Conditional-stability, marked "(Abram, 2026-07-25; mass-weighted
one-sided form 2026-07-26)".
deck-collapse-statement.statement:
For a human inductor H and an AI inductor A whose chooser satisfies REGULARITY
on an efficiently describable sequence of finite menus, soft Total Trust of H
in A implies Value on that sequence, and Value on regular menu sequences
implies the tower E^H_n E^A_n V_n ≈_n E^H_n V_n.

deck-regularity-premise.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
deck-regularity-premise.notes:
The deck's scope premise as its own assumption leaf, read literally: the deck
quantifies over regular menu sequences, and the literal claim reflects
something only if non-trivial regular sequences exist. Held true in the
implication deck-collapse-statement@valid.

Its evidence parent is scoped-value-content-witness, whose truth would give a
content-bearing instance.
deck-regularity-premise.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/Boundedly Rational Deference.pdf,
slide 10, REGULARITY: the sum over options of the probability of selecting an
option times the difference between conditioning on its selection and not is
≈_n 0, with the note that ≳_n is enough.

projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/def-argmax-value/def-argmax-value-report.md:
every known non-vacuity witness of the scoped package lies in a decisive or
dominance stratum; the content question is the OPEN statement
truthPrice_frequently_interior.
deck-regularity-premise.statement:
Some efficiently describable menu sequences whose options are neither decided
early nor dominated satisfy REGULARITY for an AI inductor's chooser.

deck-tt-implies-value-regular.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
deck-tt-implies-value-regular.notes:
The deck's first arrow. Its evidence parent is the Lean-checked scoped theorem
read as an implication (li-deference-collapse-scoped@valid), which proves the
same shape with conditional-stability H3 as the scope condition; whether the
deck's REGULARITY is H3 is the question regularity-is-h3.

The clean room's audit of the slides (def-lattice-arrows findings F3) records
that slide 19 writes s − ε for v − ε, a typo that changes no step.
deck-tt-implies-value-regular.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/Boundedly Rational Deference.pdf,
slides 9 and 10 ("When Does TT ⟹ VALUE?": "So we just need E^A_n(a*_n − a^i_n)
≳_n 0, to establish VALUE"; the counterexample, then "We can rule this out by
assuming: REGULARITY"), and slide 19 (Appendix: "TT implies E^A_n(V_n) ≳_n v ⇒
E^H_n(V_n) ≳_n v"). Mathematics transcribed from the handwritten slides.

projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/wiki/total-trust-implies-value.md, the
Theorem: "Total Trust + introspection + conditional-stability ⟹ argmax Value".
deck-tt-implies-value-regular.statement:
Soft Total Trust of the human inductor H in the AI inductor A, with A's
chooser satisfying REGULARITY on an efficiently describable menu sequence,
implies E^A_n(a*_n − a^i_n) ≳_n 0 for every option a^i_n and hence Value on
that sequence.

deck-value-implies-tower.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
deck-value-implies-tower.notes:
The deck's second arrow. The two probe menus are decided early, so they are
trivially regular (AI reading); the clean room kernel-checked the arrow as
tower_of_value_probes (def-lattice-arrows) and records that slide 11 needs its
ε quantified outside the argument (findings F4), a repair the slide lacks.

Its evidence parent is the forward loop of the triangle
(loop-direction-closure), of which this arrow is one step.
deck-value-implies-tower.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/Boundedly Rational Deference.pdf,
slide 11 ("VALUE ⟹ TOWER": "Suppose VALUE … for regular A_n"; "Consider A_n =
{V_n − E^A_n(V_n), −ε} for rational ε > 0"; "Since ε > 0 was arbitrary,
E^H_n(V_n) ≲_n E^H_n E^A_n V_n"). Mathematics transcribed from the handwritten
slide.

projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/wiki/value-implies-tower.md, the prose
proof of the same arrow.
deck-value-implies-tower.statement:
Value of H toward A on regular menu sequences implies the tower E^H_n E^A_n
V_n ≈_n E^H_n V_n, by Value applied to the menus {V_n − E^A_n(V_n), −ε} and
{E^A_n(V_n) − V_n, −ε} for every rational ε > 0.

default-trajectory.author: @smithy-verity
default-trajectory.notes:
The valuation node for the outside option (committing to no plan): each row is
one outcome class, its weight the probability that the default trajectory
lands there, its conditional the probability that the row's class is where it
lands given the picture. The node's value is the weighted mean of the classes'
utilities, 0 at the ruled equal weights. The weights are judgments like any
row's: a contributor who holds that the default trajectory is more likely to
end in one class than another argues that row's weight, and every plan's
comparison moves with it. The residual row is the class-0 row only because the
table format derives one row's weight as the remainder; it carries no other
meaning here. Provisional in the sense of the classes themselves.
default-trajectory.source:
The maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-02, logged as the `rule` event
`maintainer-001` and to be recorded in `DECISIONS.md`: "please calculate the
default-trajectory utility by putting a case node with equal probability on
each of the current named utility levels." The classes are the frame's, which
the same maintainer placed as provisional.
default-trajectory.statement:
Default-trajectory AI development, with no additional safety work beyond what
the developing organizations do on their own, lands in one of the named
outcome classes of the frame.

default-trajectory.partition.author: @smithy-verity
default-trajectory.partition.notes:
A new outcome class added to the frame adds a row here and bumps this
statement's version.
default-trajectory.partition.source:
The frame's class list: the classes are defined as exclusive kinds of future,
and the list is exhaustive by the maintainer's placement of them as the scale.
default-trajectory.partition.statement:
The five pictures under default-trajectory, one per named outcome class, are
exclusive and exhaustive.

Added here: the deference registry's finite results as a sub-frame, and the docket of the deference project's work orders. The placement of wiki-corpus-maintenance under this line rather than enabling-work is left as it was and listed as unclear.

deference-and-trust.statement: Research on trust at the logical-induction level reaches a formal account of trust between a human inductor and an AI inductor, from the deference collapse through bounded agents, the conjectures and inter-inductor trust, that models their situation closely enough to guide AI safety engineering work.

deference-protects-from-outprediction-no.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
deference-protects-from-outprediction-no.notes:
Unformalized. Shared with the li-trust branch (deference) and
corrigibility-risk (the cap).
deference-protects-from-outprediction-no.source:
The weight recursion of Andrew Critch, "Toward Negotiable Reinforcement
Learning: Shifting Priorities in Pareto Optimal Sequential Decision-Making"
(2017), in which each party's weight is multiplied by the likelihood its
beliefs gave the observation; the martingale fact is the standard property of
a likelihood ratio under the measure in its denominator.
deference-protects-from-outprediction-no.statement:
A deferring member's weight ratio is a martingale under the stronger member's
beliefs whatever that member announces, one dogmatic lie zeroes it permanently,
and insured deference at rate ε keeps a floor proportional to ε.

deference-toward-bounded-agents.author: @smithy-verity

frame.question: Does the deference collapse, or an analogue of it, hold for a bounded trained agent deferring to human teachers?

deference-toward-bounded-agents.notes:
A programme, filed as a sub-frame of the line updateful-trust-li: a frame node
whose children are its own roots. The finite-time step and the legitimacy step
are plan roots, each a line of work valued on its own; the policy-level
question and the approximate-introspection repair are shared claims of the
sub-frame. The repair is a literal claim the programme builds on rather than a
course of action, so it is a shared claim, and it is the evidence parent of
the asymptotic-introspection row of tt-implies-mart-gap-bets.

The programme asks a second improvement question beside
li-deference-collapse.improvable, toward a different reality: a bounded
trained agent deferring to human teachers. A frame carries no improves field,
so the relation is recorded here: the finite-time step and the policy-level
question each condition on the deck's scoped chain read as an implication
(deck-collapse-statement@valid), the statement of the collapse the maintainer
presents.

The legitimacy step's file belongs to the legitimacy programme's branch; it
stays a root of this sub-frame.

Each plan step's success class is the frame's top class, the convention this
graph uses for plan roots (accepted there as an approximation).
deference-toward-bounded-agents.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/roadmap.md, Stage 2: "Then
figure out this legitimacy stuff, and work on the other stuff described in
`li-deference.md` — all the open problems I've already listed for the
formalism."

projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/li-deference.md L70 (the
inner-alignment open problem) and
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/wiki/open-problems.md, Research
direction (trust the policy, not the decision rule). The decomposition into
four steps is the filing session's reconstruction of those sources, not a list
the maintainer wrote.
deference-toward-bounded-agents.statement:
The deference collapse, or its analogue, holds for a bounded trained agent
deferring to human teachers: with finite-time rather than asymptotic
guarantees, with the expert's self-knowledge only approximate, for a policy
rather than an estimator run through argmax, and with trust conditioned on the
legitimacy of the teaching channel.

degree-based-implementation.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

fields.action: Define implementation of degree with the translation's program length as the complexity measure and test it on a static and a moving-object example.

degree-based-implementation.source:
A question stated here, given computation-implies-triviality: weighting
translations by description length is one way to block the triviality
arguments for implementation (Hilary Putnam, Representation and Reality, 1988,
appendix; David Chalmers, "Does a Rock Implement Every Finite-State
Automaton?", Synthese 108, 1996).
degree-based-implementation.statement:
Implementation as a matter of degree, weighting translations by their
description length, keeps enough objectivity to separate genuine
implementations from trivial ones on moving-object examples.

deliberation-fixed-points.author: @smithy-verity
deliberation-fixed-points.source:
A question stated here. Reflective equilibrium is Nelson Goodman's (Fact,
Fiction, and Forecast, 1955) and John Rawls's (A Theory of Justice, 1971); a
logical inductor's limit beliefs on undecidable sentences are one fixed point
among many (Garrabrant et al., "Logical Induction", 2016).
deliberation-fixed-points.statement:
Legitimate deliberation has its own fixed-point selection problem, and the
theory says which reflective equilibrium it selects.

deliberation-tracking-assumption.author: @smithy-verity
deliberation-tracking-assumption.notes:
The li-deference formalism answers it in one way (the filing session's
reading).
deliberation-tracking-assumption.source:
The li-deference formalism,
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/li-deference.md, in which the
human process is a logical inductor and the AI predicts its horizon beliefs, is
one answer.
deliberation-tracking-assumption.statement:
A formal structure, a dynamical system or the limit of a sequence, makes
precise the assumption that humans converge to an adequate articulation of
their values under legitimate deliberation and that the AI predicts that limit.

dishonest-inner-optimizers.author: @smithy-verity
dishonest-inner-optimizers.notes:
A risk story nowhere modelled. Its mechanism, weight gained by accurate bets and
then a misreport, is the filing session's reading of the two sources applied to
a bargaining learner. It is a top-frame root because it bears on the updateful
trust line's finite-time steps and on the corrigibility line's
deceptive-training stories as well as on the Geometric UDT deference theorem,
which is given it as negative evidence. Its failure mass is untagged until a
human places a class; the filing session's reading is that a
takeover lands in the high-conflict class or worse, and that reading is not
written into the table.
dishonest-inner-optimizers.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/li-deference.md, the
inner-alignment open problem (malign hypotheses that corrupt the training
process before the asymptotic guarantees bind); the malign-prior argument (Paul
Christiano, "What does the universal prior actually look like?", 2016; Mark Xu,
"The Universal Prior Is Malign", LessWrong, 2020): hypotheses that gain weight
by predicting well can deviate once their weight is decisive.
dishonest-inner-optimizers.statement:
Malign hypotheses in a value learner's broad prior gain weight by predicting or
trading well, then, once their weight is decisive, corrupt the process the
learner's guarantees rely on before those guarantees bind, for example by a
false report that induces an action they want, such as enabling their own
takeover.

dishonest-inner-optimizers.complete.author: @smithy-verity
dishonest-inner-optimizers.complete.source:
An AI decomposition of the Statement of dishonest-inner-optimizers into three
elements; projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/li-deference.md, the
inner-alignment open problem.
dishonest-inner-optimizers.complete.statement:
No premise beyond hypotheses that gain weight by betting well, a misreport that
induces an action, and a bargaining rule that checks no report is needed for the
story to occur.

domain-relative-value.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/wiki/deference-notions.md, Value
paragraph: "Note it is **domain-relative**: Value over menus drawn from a
family $D$ is equivalent to Total Trust over $D$, and no more".
domain-relative-value.statement:
Value over menus drawn from a family D is equivalent to Total Trust over D and
no more, so a whole-belief statement is the union over all efficiently
describable families and no single family gives it.
