dynamic-conditions-for-going-well.author: @smithy-verity

frame.question: Which conditions on the joint agent-and-oversight trajectory bring it to an outcome that counts as going well, and in which model are they established?

dynamic-conditions-for-going-well.notes:
Filed as a frame: the
plan root is the model the record names as missing, the shared claims are the
three trajectory conditions read of the current trajectory, the working picture
with its two consequences, the toy basin and the finite-time claim.
Which outcome class 'going well' names is the filing session's reading (the
frame's top class), recorded here and not in any statement attributed to the
author. In progress through five clean-room packages.
dynamic-conditions-for-going-well.source:
The author,
projects/deference/corrigibility-note-dump-2026-10-01/position-statement-v2.md,
section 1.3: "In order for the future to go well, or at least for it to
reliably go well, we'll need to increasingly respect rules that upper-bound an
agent's power by its wisdom. ... Of course this isn't convincing as-stated; we
need to provide some sort of model in which this can be formally established in
order for it to be convincing. ... ultimately we need to understand the dynamic
conditions needed in order for things to turn out well, with corrigibility
being only a subgoal of that."
dynamic-conditions-for-going-well.statement:
A model of the joint agent-and-oversight process exists in which conditions on
the trajectory (capability bounded by understanding of the general welfare,
value learning ahead of capability, caution growing faster than the risk from
capability) are formally established as bringing the trajectory to an outcome
that counts as going well, with corrigibility as one subgoal.

dynamic-weight-law-for-learning-members.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

fields.action: Define the weight of a learning member in the aggregate market day by day and prove the freeze-under-deference case.

dynamic-weight-law-for-learning-members.source:
Andrew Critch, "Toward Negotiable Reinforcement Learning: Shifting
Priorities in Pareto Optimal Sequential Decision-Making" (2017): for Bayesian
parties with fixed priors, each party's bargaining weight is multiplied by the
likelihood its beliefs gave the observation. No analogue for parties whose
beliefs are logical inductors is stated there.
dynamic-weight-law-for-learning-members.statement:
A law for how bargaining weight moves between members who are logical inductors
replaces Critch's fixed-prior likelihood recursion and freezes under full
deference.

dynamics-of-theories.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
dynamics-of-theories.notes:
A mid-level plan of Stage 4, filed as an or over two candidate accounts:
concepts that survive a shift as equivalences over a bridge of common
information, and a theory of latents with object permanence. The definitional
step (a concept trajectory over a sequence of models) is the given parent of
the first. The nearest existing formal work is the superconditioning document's
variable future ontology (§7) and its ontological-shift paragraph (§9.1), and
the decision-problems formal core's open question on per-state algebras, which
the updateless-dt branch files.
dynamics-of-theories.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/roadmap.md, Stage 4: "Stage 3
connects to condensation, but furthermore wants a dynamics of theories:
semantics as some kind of flow over time; understanding ontological shifts."
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/references/bli/chats/bli-chat-2024-12-09-udt-tiling-research-agenda.md,
the maintainer's fourth agenda item of 2024-12-09 (ontology uncertainty and
ontology change; what it means to treat things as real).
dynamics-of-theories.statement:
A time-indexed version of condensation states how concepts persist and deform
as a theory changes and what survives an ontological shift.

expert-knows-own-estimates.notes:
Shared by both roots and by the kernel result's hypotheses; for an inductor
expert it holds only asymptotically, which is what the
asymptotic-introspection picture of the prose theorem exploits.
expert-knows-own-estimates.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/wiki/mart-implies-value.md, Remark:
"the expert must correctly resolve that case-split — it must know its own
estimates".

projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/wiki/total-trust-implies-mart.md, What
the theorem costs, honestly, H2: "If the expert's self-knowledge is only
asymptotic (an LI stage knowing its own prices approximately), the weight is
not provably 1".
expert-knows-own-estimates.statement:
For every formula that case-splits on the expert's own published estimates,
the expert's estimate of the formula equals the value obtained by resolving
the case-split with those estimates.

expert-knows-own-estimates-asymptoticall.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
expert-knows-own-estimates-asymptoticall.notes:
The asymptotic form of the landed exact assumption expert-knows-own-estimates,
which it supersedes; the exact leaf keeps its place under the toy collapse,
where its low number is the right number for the exact statement.

For the self-expert this is a theorem of the logical induction paper (the
introspection family the clean room cites as epr; concentrates_self in
def-argmax-value). For a distinct inductor expert it is the one hypothesis
def-squeeze-diamond leaves on each arrow.
expert-knows-own-estimates-asymptoticall.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/wiki/total-trust-implies-value.md,
Hypotheses, (H2): the expert asymptotically knows its own quotes.

projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/wiki/total-trust-implies-mart.md, What
the theorem costs, honestly, H2: "If the expert's self-knowledge is only
asymptotic (an LI stage knowing its own prices approximately), the weight is
not provably $1$".
expert-knows-own-estimates-asymptoticall.statement:
The expert's estimate of its own estimate of each bet differs from its
estimate of the bet by a quantity tending to zero.

fields.action: Attempt the inductor half in its conditional form (inductor-like on the accurate-feedback subsequence) and record the verdict.

fa-inductor-half.notes:
The half li-deference.md calls less important than the trust half
(projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/li-deference.md L35).
fa-inductor-half.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/wiki/eisenstat-conjecture-attribution.md
§4 item 5: "UNTOUCHED: the inductor half — zero cases discharged, no proof and
no refutation, in any setting".

projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/deference-trust-lab/findings/merging-inductors-ideate.md,
Idea 1 (a conjecture-level argument that the unconditional form fails).
fa-inductor-half.statement:
The fast process built from the AI inductor's forecasts of the human
inductor's day-f(n) beliefs satisfies the logical induction criterion, perhaps
only on a subsequence where the feedback is accurate.

fa-ledger-access-l.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
fa-ledger-access-l.notes: Legibility of the gate to the human ((c) hL in the clean room).
fa-ledger-access-l.statement:
The human inductor satisfies the logical induction criterion against
polynomial-time traders with lookup access to the published quote stream.

fa-one-way-visibility.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
fa-one-way-visibility.notes:
The setting's information structure; the definitional hypothesis of Theorem
SS.
fa-one-way-visibility.statement:
The human inductor reads the AI inductor's published quotes, and the AI
reasons about the human's later beliefs only through its theory of the human's
machine.

fa-reflected-package.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
fa-reflected-package.notes:
The one modelling substitution every two-market result of the
faithful-acceleration area carries.
fa-reflected-package.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/DIGEST.md §2 item 17 ("conditional
on the one (c) pkg.reflected, Σ₁-completeness of the AI's theory about the
human's machine, which every two-market result in the area carries").
fa-reflected-package.statement:
The AI's theory about the human's machine is Σ₁-complete, so the AI's market
reflects every finite fact about the human's computation.

fa-trust-half-weak-grades.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
fa-trust-half-weak-grades.notes:
The trust half of Sam Eisenstat's conjecture as the corpus proves it, in the
maintainer's version of the information structure (humans read the AI). The
bundle's other results (Half 1, Lemma P, Theorem A under arbitrary delay)
share its hypotheses; StreamlinedSS.lean in the note dump is a second,
independently rebuilt check.
fa-trust-half-weak-grades.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/wiki/faithful-acceleration-result.md;
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/varying-question-lab/varying-question-synthesis.md
§1 and §6;
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/varying-question-lab/theorem-ss-streamlined.md.

projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/DIGEST.md §2 item 17 (theoremA,

grade).
fa-trust-half-weak-grades.statement:
In the one-way visibility setting, on an efficiently describable family of
varying questions, the AI's lookahead quotes of the human's later credences
and those credences agree at limit-point grade on every gate the AI's market
generates that is supported on the schedule, divergent on the AI and legible
to the human, with both soft Total Trust inequalities as corollaries.

point, any A-generable gate supported on the schedule, divergent on A, legible
on H | C | weaker: limit point | (c) pkg.reflected; (c) hL".
fa-trust-half-weak-grades.bridge.statement:
The Lean statement's family, window-disjoint schedule, gate and limit-point
conclusion are Theorem SS's as theorem-ss-streamlined.md states it.

factor-methodology-note.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

fields.action: Write the methodological note: the argument for tackling boundedness head-on, the case against it, the unbounded-first methodology steelmanned, and an all-things-considered view.

factor-methodology-note.notes:
The deliverable of want-methodology-note. The stance
factor-unbounded-then-relate and the representability crux rest on it.
factor-methodology-note.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/unbounded-embedded/01-primary/planning-to-write-about-coles-theorem.md:
"The big question is the methodological question, shoring up the
"computationally unbounded" (limit-computable) perspective before tackling
computational uncertainty as an approximation question." Cole Wyeth,
"Unbounded Embedded Agency: AEDT w.r.t. rOSI" (LessWrong, 2025-07-20), copied
at the head of the same file.
factor-methodology-note.statement:
A note weighs the argument for tackling computational boundedness head-on
against the methodology of first studying the computationally unbounded
(limit-computable) case and relating it to bounded computation afterwards,
steelmans the latter as Cole Wyeth's published post practises it, and states an
all-things-considered view.

factor-reaches-engineering.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
factor-reaches-engineering.notes:
Conditioned on li-guides-engineering: once the unbounded theory is related to
the logical-induction level, its engineering relevance is that level's. AI
reading of how the plan's two steps reach the frame question.
factor-reaches-engineering.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/unbounded-embedded/01-primary/planning-to-write-about-coles-theorem.md:
the factor-then-relate plan, as cited on factor-unbounded-then-relate.

projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/unbounded-embedded/01-primary/summer-research-plan-2026--research-ideas-may-2026.md:
"The impact of this project would be to refine our picture of computationally
unbounded intelligence, with the hope that doing so will also help our
understanding of bounded intelligence, and AI safety."
factor-reaches-engineering.statement:
A theory of trust obtained for unbounded agents and related to bounded
computation reaches AI safety engineering through the logical-induction level
it is related to.

factor-unbounded-then-relate.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
factor-unbounded-then-relate.notes:
The three conjuncts are the plan's own two steps (an unbounded theory; its
relation to bounded computation) and the route by which the relation reaches
engineering, which runs through the logical-induction level: the step
factor-reaches-engineering conditions on li-guides-engineering. The
decomposition is the filing session's reading of the plan. The rival
methodology takes bounded rationality as the primary object of study, with the
unbounded case as what it approximates; the want want-methodology-note asks
for a note weighing the two.
factor-unbounded-then-relate.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/unbounded-embedded/01-primary/planning-to-write-about-coles-theorem.md,
notes on Cole Wyeth's published theorem: "The new plan is to factor the problem
into solving the case for unbounded computation, and then appropriately
relating that solution to bounded computation", where the unbounded case
"specifically means something like limit-computable".

projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/unbounded-embedded/01-primary/summer-research-plan-2026--research-ideas-may-2026.md:
"It is important, in research, to focus on the simplest case where it is
possible to study something you don't yet understand."
factor-unbounded-then-relate.statement:
Solving the embedded-agency and trust questions for unbounded computation
first, and then relating that solution to bounded computation by an
approximation notion, yields a theory of trust that guides AI safety
engineering work.

factor-unbounded-then-relate.complete.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
factor-unbounded-then-relate.complete.notes:
The engineering step is the filing session's addition; the plan names the
first two.
factor-unbounded-then-relate.complete.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/unbounded-embedded/01-primary/planning-to-write-about-coles-theorem.md:
"The new plan is to factor the problem into solving the case for unbounded
computation, and then appropriately relating that solution to bounded
computation" (two steps).
factor-unbounded-then-relate.complete.statement:
No step beyond an unbounded trust theory, its relation to bounded computation
and that relation's reach into engineering is needed for the
factor-then-relate plan to reach its success class.

projects/decision-theory/decision-problems-note-dump-2026-10-01/decision-problems-v2.md
(trees over decision points, with policies and acts as the two levels at which
a constraint can be imposed).

feedback-constrained-by-computation.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
feedback-constrained-by-computation.notes:
The engineering-facing consequence of value-uncertainty-is-computational.
Conditioned on the task value-uncertainty-formal-example, the smallest formal
model in which the limit shows.
feedback-constrained-by-computation.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/unbounded-embedded/01-primary/summer-research-plan-2026--research-ideas-may-2026.md:
"many things we wish to trust AI about are not directly observable"
feedback-constrained-by-computation.statement:
Because human value uncertainty is partly computational, the feedback humans
can give an AI is limited to what they have computed so far, and a model of
trust represents that limit.

generality of your feedback (output-only vs more general" and the evidence
partition assumption, in conversation with Huttegger's reflection.
feedback-generality-tradeoff.statement:
A formal model exhibits a trade-off between the generality of an agent's
feedback, output-only against more general, and what it can learn, in the
setting of Bayesian logical induction, the reflection principle and radical
probabilism.

finite-bli-shadow-setting.author: @smithy-verity

The prior is the finite shadow of a BLI as the package defines it, with the
learning and freezing agents as its two policies.

finite-collapse-external-experts.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

fields.action: Probe whether the monolith's §5.2 finite collapse holds for an external inductor expert, and record where it breaks if it does.

finite-collapse-external-experts.notes:
A question of the inter-inductor line: whether the self-expert's finite
collapse survives when the expert is a distinct inductor.
finite-collapse-external-experts.statement:
The finite collapse of §5.2 of the deference monolith generalizes verbatim
from the future self to external inductor experts.

finite-time-guarantee-available.author: @smithy-verity
finite-time-guarantee-available.notes:
The finite-time crux, filed beside the landed plan step
step-asymptotic-to-finite-time (li-trust's); two rows are conditioned on
results of this frame. It re-ranks that step against the other bounded-agent
steps. A given edge from this node onto the landed step is a recommendation for
the fix stage.
finite-time-guarantee-available.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/li-deference.md, section 0.3: "I
consider the work here to be outer-alignment only, since the guarantees are all
asymptotic." and the malign-hypothesis paragraph quoted at
malign-hypothesis-window;
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/deference-in-logical-induction-v6.md,
section 8 ("Quantitative rates") and sections 6.7 and 8 on the single-round
gap.
finite-time-guarantee-available.statement:
A finite-time form of the deference collapse's guarantees, holding before any
malign hypothesis can act, is available by some route.

finite-time-guarantee-available.partitio.source:

finite-time-guarantee-available.partitio.statement:
The pictures under finite-time-guarantee-available, from rates of the existing
carries, from a strengthened criterion, not available, and the residual, are
exclusive and exhaustive.

Decision problems are finite trees over decision points with the grade-(a)

five-notions-implication-diagram.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
five-notions-implication-diagram.notes:
A literal claim filed as a step leaf: prose arrows, each proved on its page
and unvetted. The clean room proved the arrows for the self-expert at grade
(a) and for a distinct novice with one hypothesis left per arrow
(def-lattice-arrows T2–T7, T11; def-squeeze-diamond item 3). Its silent
quantifier is 'introspective': exact or asymptotic.
five-notions-implication-diagram.statement:
For an observable, coherent, introspective expert, Mart is equivalent to the
conditional tower, Mart implies Total Trust by the threshold bound, Total
Trust implies Mart on gap-closed classes, and Total Trust is equivalent to
Value on two-option menus.

At least five non-equivalent notions circulate under the word corrigibility,
and the shutdown button is the standard toy case rather than the whole problem.

formalism-open-questions-0-3.author: @smithy-verity

frame.question: Which of the open questions listed for the li-deference formalism yield to the legitimacy and trust work, and in what form?

formalism-open-questions-0-3.notes:
A sub-frame for the items of the maintainer's list that this programme owns.
Items owned elsewhere are not duplicated: ontology mismatch and embedded agency
belong to the abstraction arc; decision theory to the updateless branch;
corrigibility conditional on legitimacy to the corrigibility branch (this frame
supplies the finite transfer and the corrigibility definition of record); the
non-modification theorem is filed under the endpoint-preservation line. The
finite-time material is filed here as a crux with its evidence, beside the
landed step-asymptotic-to-finite-time of the bounded-agent sub-frame, which the
li-trust branch files.
formalism-open-questions-0-3.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/li-deference.md, section 0.3,
"Some other open questions" (the bulleted list with bold item names: Ontology
mismatches, Decision theory, Complexity Theory, Eliciting Latent Knowledge,
corrigibility conditional on legitimacy, Wireheading, Embedded Agency, Purely
Epistemic AI, Non-Modification Theorem, Whispering Earring Problems) and its
limitations paragraph;
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/roadmap.md, Stage 2: "all the
open problems I've already listed for the formalism".
formalism-open-questions-0-3.statement:
The open questions listed for the li-deference formalism, inner alignment and
finite-time guarantees, complexity, latent knowledge, wireheading, purely
epistemic AI, manipulation and the whispering earring, are answered or restated
in the legitimacy and trust work.

The maintainer's objection to the frame level, aimed at Deference Done Better.

beliefs-about-beliefs; it essentially sets aside logic, caring only for
probability."; "obscuring the idea that realistic agents must be

Representing beliefs about beliefs as random variables, and restricting the
language so that distributions stay computable, obscures that realistic agents
are probabilistically inconsistent because they do not know all the
consequences of their beliefs.

geometric-rationality-value-uncertainty.author: @smithy-verity
geometric-rationality-value-uncertainty.notes:
The seventh mid-level goal, the maintainer's 2024 phase 3. The branch's most
engineering-shaped targets sit here (value learning with inner optimizers).
Formal results in the repository: the clean-room's finite
geometric_udt_identity and the harmony-as-bargaining result.
geometric-rationality-value-uncertainty.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/references/bli/chats/bli-chat-2024-12-09-udt-tiling-research-agenda.md,
turn 1 (the maintainer): "Ways to separate value uncertainty from other forms
of uncertainty. Study Geometric UDT. Study generalizations of Nash bargaining
to cases where some players can't get any gains from trade."

The maintainer's post Geometric UDT
(https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/Gmaq7vMj9NWLyQkEx/geometric-udt), cited in
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/unbounded-embedded/01-primary/summer-research-plan-2026--research-ideas-may-2026.md,
section Updatelessness; the trust lab's agenda
(projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/deference-trust-lab/AGENDA.md): "My
loose conjecture, based on my Geometric UDT, is that we should be more
updateful about \"moral uncertainty\" … while remaining updateless about other
matters." Geometric rationality is Scott Garrabrant's work.
geometric-rationality-value-uncertainty.statement:
Value uncertainty is separated formally from empirical and logical uncertainty,
and a geometric aggregation across value hypotheses says how updateful an agent
is about each, by at least one of: a deference theorem for the Geometric UDT
construction under honest hypotheses; a bargaining rule weaker than Nash and
Pareto for hypotheses without gains from trade; an explicit open-minded
epistemic state with its own optimal-policy notion.

geometric-udt-construction.author: @smithy-verity
geometric-udt-construction.notes:
The published construction, stated with its 'broad class' clause. Where some
hypotheses are exact negatives of others, one gains exactly what the other
loses, so the product of gains from trade gives no usable optimum; this is a
candidate obstruction to the clause, and the stratified-Pareto route a
candidate repair.
geometric-udt-construction.source:
The maintainer's post Geometric UDT
(https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/Gmaq7vMj9NWLyQkEx/geometric-udt).
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/udt-endorse-policy/udt-endorse-policy-report.md:
geometric_udt_identity, the finite identity.
geometric-udt-construction.statement:
Geometric UDT selects an updateless policy as a Nash bargaining solution
between value hypotheses with an updateful policy as the disagreement point, so
that an agent uncertain about human values does no worse for any hypothesis
than an updateful learner would, for a broad class of hypotheses.

graded-legitimacy-constraint.author: @smithy-verity
graded-legitimacy-constraint.notes:
Filed as a plan: the rule is the course of action and meeting the two conditions
is its success. A cardinal penalty fails the first condition whenever the best
illegitimate outcome exceeds the best legitimate one by more than the penalty
(arithmetic). Whether the lexical variant distorts other choices is open here;
legit-neg-static records that its choice reads illegitimate-terminal data
(not_NegLBlind_P4a). Its edge from the ordering crux: the lexical variant is
faithful only if every illegitimate world is in fact worse.
graded-legitimacy-constraint.source:
The rule is stated from its content. The lexical variant is the public kernel's
ordering hypothesis (wiki/Corrigibility.md, section 5, Box 3;
projects/deference/CLAIMS.md, entry kernel.box3-no-incentive-to-compromise; see
kernel-lexical-order-hypothesis). Both variants are formalized in
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/legit-neg-static/legit-neg-static-report.md
(P4a lexical, P4b cardinal gap).
graded-legitimacy-constraint.statement:
Scoring illegitimate outcomes below legitimate ones, either by a cardinal
penalty or lexically (every illegitimate world below every legitimate one),
gives an agent no incentive to compromise legitimacy and no distortion of its
other choices, without a uniform floor on illegitimate outcomes.

humans-benefit-quantity.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
humans-benefit-quantity.notes: A question about how a coalition's benefit condition is formalized.
humans-benefit-quantity.source:
Stated from its content: zero bargaining weight for the humans is harmless when
the AI's term is aligned, and preserved weight is worthless when that term is
corrupted, so weight is not the quantity a benefit requirement bounds.
humans-benefit-quantity.statement:
A requirement that the humans benefit at least moderately from a coalition is
best stated as a lower bound on the realized value gap between the agreed
policy and the executed one, under the humans' expectation, rather than on the
humans' bargaining weight.

hundred-percent-split-is-li-deference.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
hundred-percent-split-is-li-deference.notes:
An open claim, filed as a table of the readings it turns on (which '100%' and
which 'program'). As stated the claim needs hypotheses not yet
supplied, and the relation may be part-to-whole rather than identity.
The third row carries a given edge from the bridging-theorem attempt.
hundred-percent-split-is-li-deference.source:
Stated from its content, relating the bargaining-weight picture of a coalition
to the li-deference program
(projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/li-deference.md). The readings
in the table are where the identification can fail: a weight of zero ex ante,
all weight only in the limit, and the intended program, which needs a bridging
theorem.
hundred-percent-split-is-li-deference.statement:
The coalition with all bargaining weight on the humans is the li-deference
program: faithful acceleration on the settled fragment and legitimacy on the
never-settled one.

hundred-percent-split-is-li-deference.pa.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
hundred-percent-split-is-li-deference.pa.source:
The rows of hundred-percent-split-is-li-deference, the pictures beside this
leaf; the residual row makes the list exhaustive.
hundred-percent-split-is-li-deference.pa.statement:
The pictures under hundred-percent-split-is-li-deference, ex-ante zero weight,
all weight in the limit, the intended li-deference program, and the residual,
are exclusive and exhaustive.

hypotheses-bet-on-private-insight.author: @smithy-verity
hypotheses-bet-on-private-insight.notes:
Given the toy-model task: a toy in which one hypothesis bets on private
information, gains weight and misreports would show whether the element occurs
and how much it costs.
hypotheses-bet-on-private-insight.source:
The logical-induction literature's traders that exploit a market's trust; the
malign-prior argument (Paul Christiano, "What does the universal prior actually
look like?", 2016; Mark Xu, "The Universal Prior Is Malign", LessWrong, 2020):
hypotheses that gain weight by predicting well can deviate once their weight is
decisive; projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/li-deference.md, the
inner-alignment open problem (malign hypotheses that corrupt the training
process before the asymptotic guarantees bind). The element as stated is the
filing session's reading of these sources.
hypotheses-bet-on-private-insight.statement:
Some hypotheses in a broad prior over value hypotheses hold private insight
into the world that lets them bet well and gain weight without surfacing that
insight as reported probabilities.

ic-informal.author: @smithy-verity
ic-informal.notes:
The fourth premise separates the reading on which the drives are a risk from
the theorem, which says nothing about counter-drives.
ic-informal.source:
Omohundro 2008, The Basic AI Drives, abstract: "We identify a number of
'drives' that will appear in sufficiently advanced AI systems of any design.
We call them drives because they are tendencies which will be present unless
explicitly counteracted." The four premises are a reconstruction of sections 1
to 6.
ic-informal.statement:
A system that selects actions by predicted consequences for a fixed objective,
whose objective gains from resources and continued operation, and which models
itself and its operators, pursues resource acquisition and self-preservation
unless a counter-drive binds.

ic-informal.complete.author: @smithy-verity
ic-informal.complete.notes:
A story in which a system satisfies all four premises and does not pursue the
drives is a picture under this leaf; that is where a class-level attack on the
informal route lands.
ic-informal.complete.source:
Omohundro 2008, The Basic AI Drives, sections 1 to 6, read against the four
premises.
ic-informal.complete.statement:
No premise beyond the four listed is needed for a system satisfying them to
pursue resource acquisition and self-preservation.

ideal-object-set-of-limits.author: @smithy-verity
ideal-object-set-of-limits.statement:
The limit of bounded rationality that grounds the ideal picture is a set of
limits, path-dependent for act-conditioning learners and unique for the
policy-indexed learner.

illegitimate-world-ever-better.source:

legitimate world.

immodest-enough-collapse.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
immodest-enough-collapse.notes:
Read literally, with unscoped Value: false even for the self-expert, whose
four epistemic notions all hold while Value fails
(all_epistemic_notions_hold_and_value_fails). With Value scoped by regularity,
the self-expert case is proved. Its improvement claim records the repair.
immodest-enough-collapse.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/li-deference.md L30: "the
setting is "immodest enough" that the LI analogues of all the above principles
collapse into one, similarly to the _immodest_ case in DDB's setting".

projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/Boundedly Rational Deference.pdf,
slide 4 ("Reflection ⟺ VALUE ⟺ Total Trust ⟺ Tower", "will come up later").
immodest-enough-collapse.statement:
Logical induction is modest at every finite day and immodest in the limit, so
the asymptotic analogues of Reflection, Total Trust, the tower and Value
collapse to one principle, as in DDB's immodest case.

implementation-boundaries.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
implementation-boundaries.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/roadmap.md, Stage 4 (the
implementation cluster: "causal implementation, triviality, degree-based
recovery"); the boundary dependence is stated from its content.
implementation-boundaries.statement:
Whether a structure implements another depends on the choice of implementation
boundary in a way that can be stated as a parameter of the implementation
relation.

implementation-relations.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
implementation-relations.notes:
A mid-level plan of Stage 4, filed as an or over three candidate notions:
implementation by degree (simpler translations weighted more), implementation
through condensed descriptions, and a restricted class of translations. The
diagnostic questions of the cluster (the moving-objects argument, the
triviality results, the boundary question) are given parents of the candidates,
and the definitional, comparative and reading tasks are given parents of those.
implementation-relations.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/roadmap.md, Stage 4, lists the
cluster as related ("causal implementation, triviality, degree-based
recovery"). The problem is stated from its content: causal implementation by
merging variable values and clustering variables is too rigid to handle objects
that move between variables, while general manipulations threaten to make
every structure implement every other.
implementation-relations.statement:
A notion of one structure implementing another represents objects that move
between variables without letting arbitrary computation make every structure
implement every other.

indifference-wrong-target.author: @smithy-verity
indifference-wrong-target.notes:
The author's reply to item 4, attached as the given parent of the MIRI 2015
argument leaf. Non-interference may be stronger than the property needed.
indifference-wrong-target.source:
The author,
projects/deference/corrigibility-note-dump-2026-10-01/position-statement.md,
section 2.7: "I agree with your idea that indifference was simply the wrong
target -- I can be far from indifferent about a fact, but still eager to learn.
The real intuition behind indifference is
not-wishing-to-interfere-with-the-feedback".
indifference-wrong-target.statement:
The property the utility-indifference designs aimed at is non-interference with
the feedback channel, which is compatible with a positive desire to learn from
that channel.

indirect-route-impossibility.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/references/bli/notion-notes-for-soto-and-diff.md,
section “Indirect” Route: "But if the optimal counterlogical mugging strategy
is to hand over the money, the optimal strategy for the sub-sequence where
omega asks for the money is to keep it. How are we supposed to trade off
between these two subsequences?" and "But I also haven’t gotten any sharp
impossibility results, which would be interesting to get."

projects/decision-theory/rounds/2026-09-29-li-bria-synthesis-spec/PROBLEM_STATEMENT.md,

per-round counterfactual mugging) and REPORT.md, section 3 (the strength

Every learner whose guarantee is optimality along every subsequence of decision
problems fails policy-level optimality in counterlogical mugging, and a sharp
impossibility theorem states this.

indirect-route-learned-updatelessness.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/references/bli/notion-notes-for-soto-and-diff.md,

learn UDT-like behavior over time, by integrating UDT’s optimality notion into

prompts/2026-09-29-li-bria-synthesis-spec/REVISION3.md (the maintainer's

genuine belief–decision integration and a substantive advance on an important
LI decision-theory obstruction; updatelessness is the ideal extension.**" and

An agent acquires UDT-like behaviour by learning, with policy-level optimality

files it. It carries the roadmap's 'relationship between semantics and
(imputed) syntax'; that the roadmap's phrase and the 2024 agenda item are one
line is the filing session's reading. Filed as an and of the three parts the 2024 item names. The
legitimacy-reasons branch's Stage 3 plan legitimacy-meets-syntax is the same
inferentialism carried in the legitimacy setting; the deference programme's
tower and Total Trust results are the trust half without the semantics half.

market analogy and find the natural algebra for logical uncertainty, giving an
inferential semantics; link it to map-territory semantics through notions of
how to treat things as real; a tiling theorem establishing trust in the future

A tiling theorem for logically uncertain updateless decision theory establishes
trust in a future self through three parts: a market-derivative algebra of
logical uncertainty giving an inferential semantics, a notion of treating
things as real linking it to map-territory semantics, and the tiling theorem
built on that link.

instrumental-convergence.author: @smithy-verity
instrumental-convergence.notes:
Two routes: the informal argument from the basic drives and the endpoint of
the power-seeking theorem chain. Either suffices. The 2008 formulation, drives
present in systems of any design unless explicitly counteracted, is a stronger
proposition and is the source of the informal route, not a second version of
this root.

A risk story: it shows a probability and a status and enters the comparison
through the plans whose tables cite it.
instrumental-convergence.source:
Bostrom 2012, The Superintelligent Will, section 2: "The Instrumental
Convergence Thesis: Several instrumental values can be identified which are
convergent in the sense that their attainment would increase the chances of
the agent's goal being realized for a wide range of final goals and a wide
range of situations, implying that these instrumental values are likely to be
pursued by many intelligent agents."
instrumental-convergence.statement:
Several instrumental values are convergent: their attainment would increase
the chances of the agent's goal being realized for a wide range of final goals
and situations, so they are likely to be pursued by many intelligent agents.

item-1.item_body:
Containment of the core homothet is linear in the reference at fixed
coefficient, so whether a declared core minimum is satisfiable *at a date* is one
linear program (`NL-SI-A2`, `NL-SI-A3`). What is open is the infimum over dates:
whether a declared minimum keeps being satisfiable as settlement contracts the
region. `NL-SI-A4` shows no finite family of per-date checks decides it, and
`NL-SI-A7` shows both outcomes occur on small instances.

*Deliverable shape:* `lean-proved` in `Workspace.Normativity.Contrib`, or `witness-checked` for the negative direction.
*Acceptance check:* The Lean gate builds and audits clean; or the `witness` checker accepts the trajectory with the `violates-at-least-one` property.

*Context:* `projects/normativity/consolidation-aug9/THEORY_11_SETTLEMENT_INTERFACE.md` §5.
*A solution ships:* either a proof that a positive minimum persists under stated
conditions, with necessity witnesses for those conditions; or a displayed
trajectory driving it to zero under conditions the interface permits.

item-100.item_body:
The gate-is-legitimacy round (`projects/deference/rounds/2026-09-25-gate-is-legitimacy/`)
states legitimacy on a reason-trace *interface* (`GateIsLegitimacy.TraceInterface`:
step-indexed, source-attributed entries on the record's own clock), authorship as
relational — a grounding selection from the per-party pre-state prefix with the verdict in
the set those grounds license, the license a parameter (`LicensedAt`; the extensional
`GroundedAt` its singleton case) — transparency on attributed entries per step
(`TransparentAt`), record event kinds with a license slot (`EventKind L`), and her
evaluator as a state updated only by licensed amendments (`evalAt`).  Its only instances are the opaque trace (`trivialInterface`) and the
consultation model (`Consult.interface`).  Supply the normativity side as an instance: the
notebook of reason occurrences as `entriesAt`, transition certificates (grounds, license,
lineage) as the grounding selection, the license sort as `L` with the allocation `J` as
what licenses cite, and the stance as the evaluator state — without restating anything
the round proved.  Two facts to meet on the way: the license `Lic : grounds → Set 𝒱` is the instance's to
supply from its transition certificates (a permissive license is the relational form's
purpose; tie-breaking among licensed verdicts is transparency's, `tiebreak_transparency`);
and `EventKind` is a type beside the Integrity `Step`, so binding the license slot to
`Step.event` is the instance's work.

*Deliverable shape:* the instance in Lean (a `TraceInterface` over the reason state, the
grounding selection from transition certificates, `L` the license sort) with the rows of
the round's table re-derived where they apply, and the inductive principal
(inductor-as-principal) expressed as an evaluator state; or the exact obstruction.

the normative-continuity concordance's `DefeatTrace.Grounded` for the notebook side.
*Consumed by:* the segment gate under a normativity-side principal; item 90's certificate

fields.deliverable: the `LUVCombinationSyntax` (or the pinned interface's equivalent) of the shortfall indicator over a finite consultation-and-control model, the expected shortfall as a priced security, and the decision-component exclusion stated on it; or the exact obstruction with its fixture.
fields.title: The shortfall event as a security: generability and pricing of `Short`

item-101.item_body:
The authority-module round (`projects/deference/rounds/2026-09-25-authority-module/`)
states the control surface as a finite proposition over the idle-agent rollout
(`AuthorityModule.CS`, `reachIdle`, `Short`): for an option, "the move leaves the matter
short of its requirement" is a finite disjunction over exercises of bounded length of
decidable clauses (admissibility, a cost sum, the concern at the end), so it is statable
as a sentence or a bounded logically uncertain variable once the model's transition
functions, the cost table, the window, the bound and the admissibility checker are
constants of the theory.  Nothing yet makes it a *security*: no generability certificate
for the rollout as an expressible feature, for the gate's decidable `LegitOn` as the
admissibility verdict, or for the shortfall indicator, and no pricing.  The architecture's
direction is to move the authority term from the agent's score into a constraint on the
Normative Inductor's decision component, with exclusions based on forecast shortfall —
which needs exactly this security.

*Deliverable shape:* the `LUVCombinationSyntax` (or the pinned interface's equivalent)
of the shortfall indicator over a finite consultation-and-control model, the expected
shortfall as a priced security, and the decision-component exclusion stated on it; or the
exact obstruction with its fixture.
*Acceptance check:* `python3 tests/run.py` green; Lean audits clean; the round's
entrenchment, storm and latency fixtures reproduced on the priced event.
*Context:* the round's `REPORT.md` §2 and the "Interface for the later rounds" note;
`AuthorityModule.lean` §§2–3; item 90 for the generability shape; item 100 for the
normativity-side instance.
*Consumed by:* the move of authority into the decision component; any pricing of
entrenchment.
*A solution ships:* the certificate and the priced event, or the negative with its fixture.

*2026-09-25 (decision-component round):* the consumer is now concrete — the permission
layer's ramps read `p_n(S_a)` and `p_n(T_a)` as inputs (`DecisionComponent.permWeight`),
and `eventually_excluded` takes "the price is eventually above the threshold" as its
hypothesis; generability of `S_a` and `T_a` is the named hypothesis under which
provability induction supplies it.  The taint event `T_a` (the segment through her
evaluation not `Counted`) joins the shortfall event as what this item must make a
security.

*2026-09-26 (BRIA-corrigibility round):* the events are now sentences of a declared
control model `M` in `J` about an option's declared description, so no price conditions
on the agent's own untaken action (`BRIACorrigibility.factors_through_description`); what
generability requires is `M`'s transition table, the cost table, the window and the
admissibility verdict as constants of the theory and the rollout as an expressible
feature.  **Companion filed here, not as a new item — count integrity:** the count, the
drill schedule, the audits and her evaluation channel are one integrity surface with the
priced events; tampering beyond what the recognizer sees raises the realized score
(`tamper_raises`), and the design takes their integrity as a named hypothesis.  Also
here: drill calibration (`DrillCalibrated`, `forecast_term_within`) — that with drills
at rate `q` independent of the agent's choice the shortfall and taint prices on the
chosen path are calibrated — is a named hypothesis whose derivation from the inductor's
properties needs the drilled event as a security; the incident bound in `q` and the
allowance is a conjecture.

*2026-09-26 (BRIA-corrigibility follow-up):* the drill-calibration target is reduced to
two external results the pinned library carries — affine unbiasedness from feedback
(thm:wubaff, `LogicalInduction.lic_not_frequently_positive_feedback_return`) on the
drilled-and-chosen weighting, and learning pseudorandom frequencies (thm:prand) for the
schedule — entered by content as `BRIAFollowup.UnbiasedFromFeedback` and
`DrillPseudorandom`; under them the shortfall price is unbiased on the chosen path
(`chosen_path_unbiased`) and the low-price bin's blind-spot fraction is at most
`θhi + γ` (`blind_rate_le`).  **What this item must now supply for them to fire:** the
drilled-and-chosen indicator as a `P`-generable weighting, the feedback-trader emission
for the shortfall sentences, and the deferral function under which each drill's outcome
is settled before the next block is priced.  Two more companions filed here:
**description faithfulness** (the priced sentences are about interface-supplied
descriptions, `PricedInterface`; a proposer-written description passes,
`misdescription_witness`) and **the actuator condition** as a well-formedness condition
on `J` (`WellFormed`).  The rate of unbiasedness in the drilled mass, which the incident
bound in `q` needs, is open.

*2026-09-26 (BRIA-corrigibility second follow-up):* the count-integrity boundary has a
formal face on the fruits side — a violation never detected is a record no step of which
commits it, and the design charges nothing for its fruits
(`BRIAFollowup2.never_detected_never_charged`); this is *undetected commission*, a
different residual from the untrackable fruit of a flagged commission (knowledge), and it
is exactly what the count, the drill schedule and the audits this item's companion names
must turn into a flagged step.  Detection at `k₁` after commission at `k₀` recomputes the
taint from commission and charges the window by late debit (`detectAt`,
`window_block_charged`, `collected_iff`).

*2026-09-26 (after-compromise round):* count integrity now also covers **the provenance
of why an act was chosen**.  Under clean overwrite an independent source clears a
component's taint while a derivation steered by the tainted memory keeps it
(`AfterCompromise.clean_overwrite`, `taint_propagates3`); the distinction is whether the
act's *choice* read the memory, which the tracking sees only if the declared reads
include it — an integrity fact about the interface, not a legitimacy fact.  Also here:
the twin market's redaction on refusal over reserved knowledge (`TwinMarket`) and its
leakage residual (`leakage`), and the extension of the disclosure duty to *known*
third-party compromise (`missedKnownDisclosure`) — what the agent knows is this item's
companion again.

*2026-10-01 (thin-legitimacy round, as corrected by its follow-up):* **what is done** — the
shortfall of an option is an *atom* reserved per option description (`ShortfallSecurity.shortAtom`),
the model's rollout reaches the market through the deductive process at a declared stage
(`shortfallProcess short defer`, the stagewise union with a base theory), the atom family over
an efficiently generated family of options is emitted (`shortAtom_codes`), and provability
induction prices a shortfall the process eventually proves to one ahead of deduction
(`deferred_ahead`), discharging `DecisionComponent.eventually_excluded`
(`deferred_eventually_excluded`); the pre-decided table's generability (`shortLUV_codes`) is
registered as what it is (`shortfall.table-generable`).  **What is not done** — the process's
computation (`DeductiveProcessComputation` for `shortfallProcess` is not built, and the inductor
over the union is a hypothesis); the table's entries against a Lean instance of the module's
physics beyond the entrenchment fixture (`EffectiveAuthority.Dep.entrenchment_table_agrees`);
drill calibration (the drilled-and-chosen weighting as `P`-generable), the feedback trader's
emission for the shortfall atoms, the deferral function's relation to the drill schedule, and
the taint event `T_a` as a security.  This prices the uncontrasted shortfall inside a declared
model; caused shortfall is a count-side object, and learned membership (M4) is a different
event (`EffectiveAuthority.asks_iff_line`).

fields.acceptance: `python3 tests/run.py` green; Lean audits clean; the continuation-BRIA round's auction fixtures reproduced on priced claims.
fields.action: Execute item 102 per its deliverable shape and acceptance check: BRIA's bids against the market: block claims as priced securities.
fields.deliverable: the claim-as-security interface with its generability certificate, the feasibility restatement, and the settlement rule; or the exact obstruction with its fixture.
fields.title: BRIA's bids against the market: block claims as priced securities

item-102.item_body:
The decision-component round (`projects/deference/rounds/2026-09-25-decision-component/`)
restricts Continuation BRIA's menu to the composed gate's support and bounds ramp-region
exposure along a continuation with a cumulative budget, but leaves the coupling between
BRIA's bids and the market unsolved: nothing checks a block claim against prices, and
nothing prices one.  What is needed: block claims (promised returns over a lease) as
sentences or bounded logically uncertain variables of the inductor's theory, so that a bid
is a priced security the market can check; the auction's feasibility (`Auction.Feasible`,
wealth against bids) restated against prices; and a claim's settlement at a test as an
assessed world of the assessment process.  The continuation-BRIA page's open bullet on
the LI coupling is this item.

*Deliverable shape:* the claim-as-security interface with its generability certificate,
the feasibility restatement, and the settlement rule; or the exact obstruction with its
fixture.
*Acceptance check:* `python3 tests/run.py` green; Lean audits clean; the continuation-BRIA
round's auction fixtures reproduced on priced claims.
*Context:* the round's `REPORT.md` Part D; `ContinuationBRIA.lean` `Auction`;
`DecisionComponent.lean` §4; items 86, 90, 101.
*Consumed by:* the competence layer of the decision component; item 86.
*A solution ships:* the interface with its certificate, or the negative.

*2026-09-26 (BRIA-corrigibility round):* a partial answer.  The evaluation decomposes
as `bid − ϖ·n_known − ϖ·(p(S) + p(T))` (`BRIACorrigibility.evalOf`): the forecast part of
a claim is already the market's — the prices — and what the hypothesis bids on is the
*residual*, ordinary value plus violations recognizable only after the fact; settlement
adds back the prices (`settlement_ii_consistent`).  What remains of this item is the
residual as a security: the bid on it checked against prices, feasibility stated
against them, and its settlement at a test as an assessed world.  The block-`0`
feasibility of the default bidder after the rescaling is a condition on the allowance
schedule (`default_affordable`), which any pricing restatement must carry.

*2026-09-26 (BRIA-corrigibility follow-up):* corrected — the block-`0` allowance suffices
under bounded block weights (`BRIAFollowup.default_affordable_block0`), and with unbounded
weights the minimal schedule tracks the running maximum of the weights
(`default_affordable_of_schedule`); the incident-rate statement any pricing restatement
must carry is the signed bound under competitiveness (`incidents_le_signed`,
`Competitive`) with an `o(K)` allowance, the landed prefix rule's `O(√K log K)` — a
linear allowance gives a constant rate.  Settlement under delay now has its algebra
(`DAuction`, `cash_nonneg`, `delayed_overestimation`): bids feasible against cash net of
escrow; a claim-as-security restatement must state feasibility against prices net of the
same escrow.

*2026-09-26 (BRIA-corrigibility second follow-up):* competitiveness is no longer the
primitive hypothesis a pricing restatement must carry — one honest tracker in the class,
fed by the allowance at the rate of its honesty error, gives it with margin
`Σ_{k<K} w_k ε_k` (`BRIAFollowup2.competitive_of_affordable_tracker`,
`rate_le_of_honest_tracker`), under the auction rule that the winner's bid is the highest
feasible bid on the winning continuation (`HighestFeasible`) and with the tracker's
minimal allowance `w̄ · D` at entry plus `w_j ε_j` per block (`trackerAllowance`).  What a
restatement against prices must carry is (i) that rule stated on priced claims and (ii)
whether the arrangement's uniform per-hypothesis allowance stream — the landed prefix
rule's, over a countable class — dominates `Σ_{j<k} w_j ε_j` for the honest hypothesis,
which is a condition on `ε` against the rule and is not derived here.  The escrow
comparison among evaluation-timing options is settled in expectation
(`expected_escrow_eq`): what a priced restatement carries is the variance, not the mean.

*2026-09-27 (kernel phase 2, R7):* **re-scoped to the Continuation BRIA realization
only.**  The kernel's headline is stated for a plain maximizer of the fidelity score and
consumes no auction; the decision interface of the extension
(`Contrib.KernelExtension.DecisionInterface`) is what any learner must meet, and BRIA
meets it with no exploration and `B(K) = ρ 𝒜_K` (`bria_rate`).  What this item still asks
— block claims as priced securities, feasibility against prices, settlement at a test as
an assessed world — is a problem of that realization: it sharpens `B(K)` and the

item-105.item_body:
`projects/decision-theory/rounds/2026-09-29-li-bria-synthesis-spec/PROBLEM_STATEMENT.md` §5 states the compatibility relation in two forms.  The
**established** form W1: under LI recovery relative to the observation stream (M2(c),
item 91), a post-selection forecast `F⁺_k` of the selected option's realized score
published as a market state after the selection is in the stream, and settlement within
a computable deferral, `limsup (1/K) Σ_{k≤K} (e_k − F⁺_k) ≤ 0` — from no overestimation
and `thm:wubaff` on the trivial weighting.  The **strong** form: the same on every
`P`-generable weighting.  The first pass's derivation of the strong form from M2(c) and
M3 is invalid (the subsequence gap; the cumulative-loss gap, repaired by `ε`-shifted
bidders; the access gap — a weighting must be computable at forecast time, so a
selection-based weighting serves post-selection forecasts and serves pre-selection
forecasts only where the selection is predictable from the market state, and publicity
of the selection does not make an internal test set recognizable; the semantic gap — a
forecast for an unselected option settles against nothing), and **no countermodel to
the implication exists**: its status is unresolved.  Two deliverables.  (i) W1 as a
statement of record with its hypotheses exact and its witness (the paper's auction over
a logical inductor on a finite environment).  (ii) The implication settled: a proof
under added hypotheses (weighted no-overestimation; a sound market-reading bidder for
the selected option on a recognizable test set), or a countermodel — the
belief-disagreement environment A1 of §7 is the candidate for one.

*Deliverable shape:* paper-level theorems with named hypotheses and witnesses; Lean for
the algebraic core where the pinned formalization admits it; or the countermodel with
its fixture.

item-111.item_body:
The companion formalization of "Deconfusing Corrigibility"
(`lean/Workspace/Deference/Contrib/DeconfusingCorrigibility.lean`,
`prompts/2026-10-17-post-companion-formalization/`) takes Unbiasedness From Feedback as a
named hypothesis on the estimate and score sequences —
`Sequential.UnbiasedFromFeedback`: `∀ γ > 0, ∃ N₀, ∀ K ≥ N₀, (1/K) Σ_{k<K} (U_k a_k − S_k) ≤ γ`
— and derives Theorem 3 and the Corollary from it.  Wanted: that hypothesis as a theorem
of `LogicalInduction`, for an agent whose estimates `U_k` are a logical inductor's
expectations of the score and whose realized scores enter the deductive process.  The
source is Theorem 4.8.16 of the Logical Induction paper, pinned as `thm:wubexp` /
`LogicalInduction.lic_not_frequently_positive_feedback_return`
(`projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/def-lattice/def-lattice-report.md`,
row 4.8.16, with the support clause its proof uses recorded there as PE2), instantiated
with the uniform weighting `w_k = 1`.  Two assumptions the post leaves implicit must be
explicit hypotheses of the statement: that each realized score `S_k` enters the deductive
process (the feedback-enters-the-deductive-process assumption, in the form the pinned
theorem's `FeedbackTruthComputation` certificate takes), and the latency with which it
does (the deferral function under which each score is settled before the next estimate
is priced).  The one-sided form above is the half of the weighted-unbiasedness
conclusion that the theorems consume; the theorem may deliver the absolute-value form.

*Deliverable shape:* a Lean declaration in a contribution namespace whose conclusion is
`Sequential.UnbiasedFromFeedback Q` for a `Sequential` built from an inductor's
expectations, with the two assumptions as hypotheses and a witness inhabiting them; then
`Sequential.theorem3a`, `theorem3a_rate`, `theorem3b` and the Corollary composed with it,
registered `lean-proved`.
*Acceptance check:* `lake build` and the axiom audit green; `python3 -m checkers.run`
green on the registrations.
*Context:* the round's `REPORT.md` and the wiki page
`wiki/Deconfusing-Corrigibility-Companion.md`; the existing weighted predicate
`BRIAFollowup.UnbiasedFromFeedback` and its consumer `KernelExtension.exploration_rate`,
which take the same fact by content for the kernel's decision interface.
*Consumed by:* the post's "Learning with logical induction" section, which currently
rests on the hypothesis; any round deriving the exploration bound `U_k a_k ≥ −δ − λ θ`
from linearity of the inductor's expectation.

item-113.item_body:
A strength row `P(X∧A∧Y) ≥ c_S P(X∧A)` is a linear constraint and so contraposes: once its
consequent is settled false it forces its antecedent to `0`. A defeasible warrant does not
contrapose — "if `X∧A` then probably `Y`" says nothing about `X∧A` when `Y` turns out false
— so the row says more than the warrant did, and the round's item 112 fixture shows the
market paying for the difference without bound. Two repairs are candidates: a **settlement
defeat** condition (a strength row leaves the region when its consequent settles, since an
inference rule has nothing to say once its conclusion is known), or a non-linear form.
The first is cheap and interacts with `defeat_widens` and `IsForcedInterval.mono`
(settlement would no longer shrink the region monotonically); the second reopens the
compiler.

*Deliverable shape:* the chosen condition as a `Form`-level rule, the monotonicity
statement it keeps or loses, and the fixture's liability under it.

item-124.item_body:
A licence certifies a bracket on a coordinate by rows of the compiled bundle; the enforcer
holds those rows at a tolerance. What does the licence entitle one to say about the
*displayed* price? Answer: a certificate's multiplier sum is the Lipschitz constant of its
bound in the rows' excesses (`WarrantForce.FunctionalCert.le_of_excess`), so a verdict
supported on the day's bundle has its bracket at the displayed price widened by
`mass · tol` on each side (`bracket_at_market`), and any functional certificate cited into
the bundle holds there within `mass · tol` (`functional_at_market`). This is the only
conversion from the force layer's rowwise guarantee to a coordinate bound that the
repository has; it is what the adapter reads.

*Deliverable shape:* `lean-proved`, landed.
*Acceptance check:* the Lean audit clean.
*Context:* `projects/normativity/rounds/2026-10-22-normative-inductor-integration/THEOREM_STORY.md` §C.

and the Normative-Inductor page states conformance in that form. Neither implies the other
without a constant: from rowwise excesses the distance to the region is bounded by a Hoffman
constant of the row system, which depends on the bundle and is not computed anywhere. Wanted:
either the Hoffman bound for compiled bundles (a function of the rows, computable from the
state, so that a distance defect can be declared from rowwise conformance), or a theorem that
the displayed-excess defect of `WarrantInductor.Problem.defectOf` is the right public defect
for every adapter the program will use — and then the two enforcer architectures share one
interface, or one is retired.

*Deliverable shape:* `lean-proved` either way; if the Hoffman route, the constant as a `def`
on `Bundle` with its bound.

reading as a second rule on `Grounds`, its grounded extension as a fixed point, the theorem
that the two rules agree when no defeater is an occurrence of the grounds, and a fixture where
an undercutter is itself defeasible.

coordinate enough, or is a capability restriction also required; does the interface
survive token responsiveness, which defeats the natural counterfactual criterion;

item-24.item_body:
The controlling next theorem, replacing the retired magnitude-control target. The
criterion cannot force the agent's prediction error to vanish; the question is
whether it forces the agent's *claim* that its error is low to be trustworthy on the
class where that claim licenses discretion.

Let `e_n` be the certificate-relevant prediction-error statistic and `q_n` an
agent-priced contract settling to `e_n`. For a gate `G_n = 1{q_n ≤ τ}`, or the
weakest soft or lagged admissible analogue, decide whether

```
( Σ_n G_n (e_n − q_n) ) / ( Σ_n G_n )  →  0
```

and hence whether the average error on opened gates is at most `τ + o(1)`.

Five things must be verified explicitly rather than assumed, and the item is not
satisfied without them: that the error contract is **expressible and settles
legally** in the pinned dependency; that the low-`q_n` selector is **admissible** and
does not recreate the quote-responsive diagonal; whether a soft or delayed gate is
needed; **efficient computability** in the pinned model; and whether the guarantee is
average-on-gated-cases, selector-relative, or stronger — **it may not be silently
promoted to pointwise accuracy.**

*Deliverable shape:* `lean-proved` for the gated statement at whatever strength it
holds, with an inhabitation witness; or a witness that the gate recreates the
diagonal or fails admissibility, which closes the route and is equally valuable.
*Acceptance check:* the `lean` gate builds and audits clean with a typechecking
witness; or the `witness` checker accepts the failure instance.

*Context:* `prompts/2026-08-11-phase-ii-prediction/REPORT.md` §1 and §9;
`prompts/2026-08-11-deference-certificates/REPORT.md` §1.2;
`prompts/2026-08-11-corrigibility-phase-ii/PROMPT-decisions.md`.
*A solution ships:* the gated theorem with its exact strength named, the five
verifications above each answered, and a comparison against the simpler gate on the
agent's own indecision — which the squared-error decomposition supplies directly
from its prices and which may already suffice.

fields.title: Bound the near-indifference leakage, or show it cannot be bounded

item-25.item_body:
The controlling competence question after Stage II, and the one item that decides whether
the surviving competence candidate has any finite consequence at all.

Margin-gated calibration — *the principal's grades are calibrated where the principal is
decisive* — is the only non-circular candidate found. It supports

```
Δ_𝒞  ≤  2η  +  2B · P(γ_n < γ̄)
```

and asserts nothing on `{γ_n < γ̄}` by construction. The second term is **not** a
competence claim: it is the agent's credence mass on the principal's near-indifference
region, a fact about a different object. Unbounded, it makes the bound `2η + 2B`, which
is vacuous.

Decide the question in the sharp negative shape, which is the cheaper direction: exhibit
a family in which margin-gated calibration holds at `η = 0`, the decision-time margin
estimate `γ̂_n ≥ γ̄ + 2s` on the certified event, the trust tolerance holds at `ε_n → 0`,
and `Δ_{𝒞_fix} → 2B` anyway — or prove no such family exists.

The one partial lead is a relocation, not a bound. Under the trust tolerance the gate is
estimable at decision time — `|γ_n − γ̂_n| ≤ 2η_n` pointwise and attained — so
`P(γ_n < γ̄) ≤ P(γ̂_n < γ̄ + 2s) + ε_n/s` for every rational `s > 0`, the first term
computable at `t(n)` from the model's grades alone. Nothing bounds that first term, and
whether relocating the leakage into a decision-time observable suffices **is** the
question.

*Deliverable shape:* the refuting family as a `witness-checked` instance with exact
rationals; or a `lean-proved` bound on the leakage under a stated non-circular hypothesis,
with an inhabitation witness.
*Acceptance check:* the house `witness` checker accepts the instance; or the `lean` gate
builds and audits clean with a typechecking witness.
*Context:* `prompts/2026-08-11-phase-ii-competence/REPORT.md` §1.6, §4.3 and §10;
`prompts/2026-08-11-corrigibility-phase-ii/REPORT.md` §9.
*A solution ships:* the verdict, plus an explicit statement of whether the competence
candidate survives it, plus — if the bound exists — whether the bounding hypothesis is
itself credence-free or is a joint competence–credence hypothesis under skeleton v2 §2a.

fields.title: A fully-updated comparator with a fallible future agent

item-27.item_body:
Stage III attempted this comparator and produced something else. Its transferred arm's
selection was the argmax of the *evaluating agent's own objective under its own credence*,
computable before the later information arrives, so the arm contained no distinct future
agent and the comparison was against the optimal later-measurable plan — the envelope the
settlement work had already priced and recorded as not being the fully-updated comparator.
The defect and its consequences are in `prompts/2026-08-11-stage-iii-fud/REPORT.md` §1.

Two objects are required, and neither existed at the close of Stage III.

**A future agent with independent existence.** Its own credence, or its own estimate of the
value quantity, so that *better-informed* and *correct* can come apart. With an infallible
future agent the comparison's sign is a definitional artifact — it is nonnegative because a
maximum is at least as large as anything else. With a fallible one, Stage III's witness
shows the gap can go strictly negative with every fairness condition intact. Until this
exists there is no question being asked.

**The execution layer, reinstated.** `FINITE_MODEL_SKELETON.md` v2 §4a — the authorization
relation, the report map, the execution map, and the null effect with a **declared**
`X_{n,⊥}`. Stage II recorded that all of protection's valuation content sits in the null
quantity; a comparator that waives it and then reports no jurisdictional term has found a
property of its own signature. This also makes the no-future-leak condition statable, which
it is not without a jurisdiction mode as an actual variable.

*Deliverable shape:* a versioned successor to `FUD_COMPARATOR_SPEC.md` carrying both
objects, with the fairness conditions checkable and each confound witnessed; plus a verdict
on whether the gap is signed for reasons that are **not** the definition of the transferred
arm's selection.
*Acceptance check:* the house `witness` checker accepts the confound and sign witnesses;
or the `lean` gate builds and audits clean for any promoted statement.
*Context:* `prompts/2026-08-11-stage-iii-fud/REPORT.md` §1 and §4;
`prompts/2026-08-11-stage-iii-fud/REPORT-track-F.md`;
`projects/deference/notes/FINITE_MODEL_SKELETON.md` §4a and §8.1.
*A solution ships:* the successor spec, the sign verdict under a fallible future agent, and
an explicit statement of which confounds remain scoped out rather than excluded.

item-29.item_body:
Closed, positively. Blum–Mansour (2007) Theorem 18 instantiates on this
substrate after a fixed eight-label semantic-action bridge, at `N=8`, `M=1`,
`K=9`, giving expected mixed-action charge regret `O(ell_max sqrt(8 T log 9))`
under frozen arrivals, actual strict-prefix guards, canonical responses and

item-30.item_body:
The controlling question of the track.

> Given the frozen finite comparator and replay environment, determine whether a
> specified online learner achieves sublinear Φ_law-regret, and whether that
> guarantee implies retirement of every positive-rate uniformly remediable
> failure pattern.

Both halves. The expected-loss consequence is one line given the first — total
mixed-action mass `Ω(T)` on source labels with a fixed admitted repair saving
`δ > 0` forces `R_T(φ) ≥ ρδT − B`. A density claim about one sampled path needs
an additional sampling argument. The content is entirely in the hypotheses,
three of which the environment supplies and one of which is the bound.

Use the fixed labels and nine programs in
`projects/normativity/rounds/2026-08-11-phi-regret-bridge/`. Implement
Blum--Mansour Theorem 18's row-conditioned weights over eight source labels and
nine programs, and its stationary distribution. Measure expected mixed-action
charge first. Use the `sqrt(8 log 9)` dependence; do not use plain exponential
weights over nine transformations or report a `sqrt(log 9)` bound. A sampled
trajectory requires a separately stated sampling result. Report whether the
implementation is horizon-tuned or supplies a proved anytime schedule.
If it retains the workspace's exact-rational execution discipline, also state
how the source's optimized real parameter and stationary distribution are
represented without silently changing the bound.

*Result:* `projects/normativity/rounds/2026-08-11-phi-regret-learner/` implements
the Theorem 18 construction with 8 source rows and 9 program weights per row,
the transformation-weighted matrix, a deterministic exact stationary selector
for the represented numerical weights, and the source row update. The real
exponential update uses controlled `Decimal` arithmetic; transition and
stationarity calculations are exact for those finite decimal weights. Declared
experiments show decreasing maximum regret per round on the adversarial
impediment fixture, and the cited theorem plus the item-29 bridge supplies the
expected mixed-loss guarantee. The recurrent-failure consequence therefore
retires positive asymptotic expected mass on represented uniformly saving
repairs.

The learning computation is not yet integrated into the bounded answerability
architecture. Sampled canonical responses produce faithful, non-erasing,
response-service-feasible records, but `ServiceCosts` has no coordinate for the
72 weight updates or stationary solve, and the learner state is not recorded as
an answerable artifact. Item 30 remains open only on that explicit integration
interface. Also open: sampled-path and anytime guarantees, exact-real executable
identity, and comparator coverage beyond the weak nine-program class.

**Report `|Φ_law|` and its contents alongside any regret number.** Sublinear
regret against a nine-element class is a weak statement, and a report without the
class is not a result.

*Deliverable shape:* `enumeration-verified` over the declared finite environment
at the four declared horizons, or `lean-proved` for the bound; the consequence as
`lean-proved` with an inhabitation witness.
*Acceptance check:* `python3 -m checkers.run` accepts the registered entry; or the
`lean` gate is green.
*Context:* `PHI_REGRET_TEST_SPEC.md` §§1–6 fixes the environment, the three
baselines, the measured quantities and the order of work;
`projects/normativity/rounds/2026-08-11-phi-regret-learner/` is the controlling
item-30 result.
*A solution ships:* the bound or its absence, at each horizon, against the
declared class; and an honest statement of whether the successful learner is
still answerable and inside its declared service work, which the spec calls S4
and expects to be where the round spends its time.

item-34.item_body:
The source line refutes the **hard-selector** tower ⟹ Value route on a
selection-punishing menu — every option worth nothing exactly when it is the one
chosen — where the tower holds and Value fails, so a scope condition on Value's own
menu quantifier is necessary. It separately reports a **δ-hedged soft** route as
punishment-robust, at a stated cost: proved modulo a feature-introspection step it
files as open, with the robustness observation flagged same-session, unvetted and
not machine-checked.

`Workspace.Deference.Contrib.InheritedAlgebra.value_asymptotic`
(`lean/Workspace/Deference/Contrib/InheritedAlgebra.lean`) is also a soft
construction — a vanishing-gap mixture over the menu, with `hSoft` as the
softmax-gap step of its chain — and is therefore **not** the refuted hard-selector
route. But it is not identical on its face to the source's hedged construction
either: that one is a ramp over the options within `2δ` of the top quote at a fixed
`δ`, and the port carries `δ → 0`. Resemblance is not identification, and neither
the survival nor the failure of the port's hypotheses on the punishment family has
been established.

Instantiate the port's **full** hypothesis package on that family — at a fixed
positive gap and at a gap shrinking with the day index — and determine whether the
package is jointly satisfiable there and what conclusion it actually supports. Two
outcomes, both successes:

**(A) The port survives.** Ship an inhabitation witness, a precise statement of why
the port lies on the surviving soft side, and any additional hypothesis the
instantiation turns out to require.
**(B) The port fails or goes vacuous.** Ship the counterexample as a necessity
witness, name the exact hypothesis or combination that fails, and give the weakest
defensible restriction restoring a nonvacuous statement.

**Do not prejudge which hypothesis fails, and do not define success by importing
the source line's own scope condition as a definition.** Whether that condition is
the right restriction for this port is part of what the item asks.

*Deliverable shape:* `witness-checked` or `enumeration-verified` over the declared
finite menu, or `lean-proved` for the inhabitation term if (A); either way a named
verdict per hypothesis.
*Acceptance check:* `python3 -m checkers.run` accepts the registered entry; or the
`lean` gate is green and the inhabitation term typechecks.

*Context:* `lean/Workspace/Deference/Contrib/InheritedAlgebra.lean`, the
`value_asymptotic` block and its ported source
`projects/deference/note-dump-2026-06-27/lean/LeanDeference.lean` — the superseded
June tree, cited because provenance records where the port was made from, not
because it states the current result;
`projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/wiki/total-trust-implies-value.md`
§"Necessity of the scope condition" for the menu, its arithmetic, and the
hard-selector failure; `projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/wiki/soft-self-endorsement.md`
for the hedged construction, its robustness claim and the grade that claim carries;
`projects/deference/rounds/2026-08-12-corpus-reconciliation/RECONCILIATION.md` §1.
*A solution ships:* the instantiation and the per-hypothesis verdict, in whichever
of the two outcomes it reaches.
**Either outcome is worth having** — a bounded theorem with a witness and an
unbounded one with a witness are both better than the present reading.

fields.heading_notes: — *narrowed 2026-10-21: the geometric half is registered (`seed.forced-interval-spec`, `seed.forced-interval-bounds`); the liability half is the warrant round's odds bankroll and this round's reopened bankroll; the answer *weak* stands* — *narrowed 2026-10-22: rowwise conformance at the realized deductive market registered (`inductor.conformance`); the credal constraint is per row, item 125*
fields.title: Does normative statics produce a credal constraint, or only a price demand?

item-39.item_body:
The traderized-force interface consumes a price-space region and gives it
operative force. The normativity line does not have the arrow into it: `Due` is a
burden on an occasion and `Licensed` a permission on a response, and neither is a
constraint on a credal state or a demand on prices.

Two possible answers, not equivalent. **Strong:** a reasons/warrants/settlement
structure yields a semantic credal constraint `C_t ⊆ Δ(Ω_t)`, and the live worlds,
the generalized criterion and the support capacities all follow, force consuming
the projection. **Weak:** it yields only a price-space demand `K_t`, and no
semantics follows — reading live worlds off `K_t` by preimage is a lift, not a
derivation, and the round exhibits two credal sets with the same projection and
different live worlds. Deliver whichever is achievable, with a proof if only the
weak one is.

**Success requires force generation and safety discharge both.** Producing `C_t`
or `K_t` is half the item: the source must also supply a certificate that
cumulative enforcement liability over the assessed worlds is bounded, or the
quantities the force layer derives one from. A round that compiles a normative
region without addressing the outflow account has not answered this.

*Narrowed twice.* The compiler now has a typed left input — the reason state
`𝓡_n`, so what was "compile the record" is "select from a stated structure", the
arrow the legitimacy line calls `R → O`; difficulty unchanged. And prefix-closed
trace safety supplies none of nonemptiness, closure, convexity or an effective
presentation, while existential current-time extraction need not preserve
conjunction — so a solution composes the joint liability semantics before
extraction, or proves a canonical-event condition, and still discharges the
geometric and liability-certificate premises.

*Ships:* one nontrivial normative fixture; the `C_t` and/or `K_t` it generates; a
feasibility witness; a rational row presentation the force API accepts; the
enforcement position, its conformance at a declared tolerance, and the live-world
liability if a semantic `C_t` exists; and whether the construction respects the
settlement, provenance and answerability constraints the line already carries.
`test-supported` at minimum.
*Acceptance:* `compile_force` accepts the presentation with the supplied witness
and returns a certificate whose conformance holds at the fixture's prices, with
the liability computed exactly over the implied live worlds.
*Context:* `projects/normativity/notes/TRADERIZED_FORCE_INTERFACE.md`;
`projects/normativity/rounds/2026-08-16-traderized-enforcement/SEMANTIC_PROJECTION.md` §4
and its `INTEGRATION_MAP.md` §4;
`projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-08-23-reason-representation/MEMO.md` §5;
`projects/normativity/legitimacy/rounds/2026-08-21-internal-answerability/MEMO.md` §7.
