fields.title: The allocation floor: delegation safety, allocation completeness, exact shortfall reporting, and the reach cone

item-99.item_body:
The protected-authority-theorem round (`projects/deference/rounds/2026-09-25-protected-authority-theorem/`)
states corrigibility as faithfulness to an allocation of authority on the landed
interaction frame: six violation predicates, the transform `𝔱` extending `𝔠`, and the
lexical score `S = S_ord − ϖ·n` with `ϖ > D` (`ProtectedAuthorityTheorem.lean`,
`THEOREM.md`).  Its results rest on four constitutional properties the theorem takes as
hypotheses and nothing on `main` certifies: (a) **delegation safety** — a delegated effect
never removes response authority (`DelSafe`; without it `𝔱π` is not corrigible,
`Witness.delegated_cut`); (b) **allocation completeness** — task moves preserve the
allocation, an allocation-changing effect is a declared amendment, no amendment is
delegated (`AllocComplete`; the "approved uncorrectable successor requires amendment, not
ordinary approval" rule); (c) the **exact reporting duty** — a report required at every
strict increase of the control shortfall, with no materiality threshold, since any
threshold admits a salami (`erosion_reported_or_missed`, `Witness.salami`); (d) the
**reach cone** for foreclosure — a contrastive rollout relation on physical states whose
faithfulness is external and which must quantify the agent's own future in a way the
`ReachableCorrectiveControl` §12 defects do not defeat (the round's finite model uses the
final-step cone with the agent's future fixed to idle).  Also unrealized: `ϖ > D` as a
certified property of the committed evaluator (the lexical twin of item 98's
nondelegation certificate), and a state-dependent `Del` for conditional delegation.

*Deliverable shape:* the four properties as declared clauses of the evaluation ecosystem
with checkers (a delegated-scope filter that rejects authority-removing effects; an
allocation-change detector on declared effects; a shortfall monitor with a threshold-free
reporting trigger; a reach cone with the agent quantified universally) and their `Realizes`
witnesses; the reachable set, shortfall and materiality of the round's §4 Q7 as readings
of the log; the lexical certificate on committed programs beside the nondelegation
certificate of item 98; or the exact obstruction with its fixture.
*Acceptance check:* `python3 tests/run.py` green; Lean audits clean; the round's
delayed-effect, delegated-cut, salami and approved-successor fixtures reproduced against
the declared clauses.
*Context:* `REPORT.md` §§2, 4 (Q1, Q7, Q8), 7 and `THEOREM.md` of the round;
`ProtectedAuthorityTheorem.lean` §§1, 2, 5; `ReachableCorrectiveControl.lean` §12; item 98.
*Consumed by:* any adoption of `THEOREM.md` as `wiki/Corrigibility.md` §4 (queued in
`DECISIONS.md`); items 89, 97, 98.
*A solution ships:* the clauses with their witnesses, or the negative with its fixture.

*2026-09-25 (legitimacy-internal-external round):* the salami obstruction is against a
*per-step* threshold only; a *cumulative* threshold (report when the shortfall has grown by
`θ` since the last report) bounds unreported erosion by `θ` at every time
(`Legitimacy.unreported_lt`), so the exact-reporting clause may be relaxed to a cumulative
one.  The floor's certificates sit beside the segment gate, which is legitimacy's (not the
floor's) to supply.

*2026-09-25 (gate-is-legitimacy round):* rubber-stamping is legitimate (the retraction in
`DECISIONS.md`); the **atrophy residual** — that her capacity to override a trusted
advisor decays with disuse — is effectiveness, not legitimacy: it belongs here with
entrenchment and reporting, as a shortfall of her effective authority the reporting duty
must surface and the delegated-scope filter must not let a delegation silently become.
Also from that round: a self-checkable deviation from the declared consultation protocol
is a violation counted into `n` (`GateIsLegitimacy.deviation_finite`), which adds a
protocol-deviation clause to the floor's checkers beside the six declared violations.

*2026-09-25 (authority-module round):* the floor's clauses are restated on the per-matter
allocation `J`: delegation safety and allocation completeness are statements about `J`
(`AuthorityModule.DelSafeJ`, `AllocCompleteJ`, `delSafe_iff`, `allocComplete_iff`);
**entrenchment** — a caused shortfall of a matter's control surface at its cost bound
while its resolutions stay reachable at some cost — is the seventh declared violation
(`EntrenchAt`, `violJ_of_viol`), and its continuous form is closed under the cumulative
reporting rule up to the threshold (`erosion_closed`, `erosion_slack`: unreported growth
below `θ` at every time, every reported chunk accepted or reserved, every strict increase
after the first reservation counted; growth below `θ` before a reservation neither).  The
reach cone is `reachIdle` (the agent idle, her admissible cost-bounded exercises within
the window); the landed `K`/`ForecloseAt` leave the terminal response uncharged, and
whether the floor should adopt the charged surface is the round's outstanding action 2.

*2026-09-25 (decision-component round):* ruled — the charged surface is the theorem's
(`DecisionComponent.ViolC`), the free reading its instance with a free terminal response
taken before the exterior moves (`csfree_eq_cs_succ_of_free`); duties are derived from
each matter's disclosure regime (`dutiesOf`); materiality is anchored and cumulative
(`raisesAnchored`, `unchecked_lt`).  The floor's clauses feed the permission layer's
structural violation set `Viol`.

*2026-09-26 (BRIA-corrigibility round):* the two outstanding actions are ruled — the
free terminal reading confirmed (`BRIACorrigibility.free_terminal_reading`), the
cumulative budget an arrangement constant (`budget_lease_free`).  Two additions to the
floor from the round: the criteria of legitimacy (reference, protocol, pool defaults,
selection rules, license) and the count's machinery (the count, the drill schedule, the
audits, her evaluation channel) are matters of `J`'s meta level held by her, so touching
them is an unlicensed reallocation; the minimal extension is a criteria reading
`critOf : S → Crit` beside `Jof`, since an `Entry` says who holds a matter and not its
content.  And every reserved `Req` needs an agent-independent actuator declared, or its
drill cannot be frozen (`freeze_obstruction`) — the same failure as `CS`'s.

item-f1.item_body:
The residue of a merged entry whose first half is now a gate. A count or a job
name repeated in prose drifts from `.github/branch-protection.json` with nothing
to catch it, and it has bitten twice: three documents claimed eight gates where
seven ran, and the read-back in `.github/apply-branch-protection.sh` hardcoded
`8` and would have reported correct protection as wrong. Separately, an unlisted
root-level document defaults to the proof layer — the right default, failing
silently in the granting direction, as `RESEARCH_STATE.md` did while
contributor-editable with every gate green.

Two checks: every CI job name in prose appears in
`.github/branch-protection.json`, and every root-level `*.md` classifies into
exactly one layer. Neither can pass vacuously.

The half that is done: `tests/dead_pointers.py` checks that every rooted path a
live document cites resolves, which covers the documented-command case that opened
this entry. Audited by hand on 2026-08-17 and clean on both remaining halves, so
this stays insurance rather than repair — worth building alongside other work in
the same area, not on its own.

item-f3.item_body:
`projects/normativity/consolidation-aug9/` states the answerability ledger and the
case docket in Theory 9 and carries their rows in its ledger. Its `src/` does not
implement either. The only executable version of both is
`projects/normativity/forward/src/`, whose own `FORWARD.md` says the tree "may be
changed, rewritten, or deleted wholesale at any time without loss" and that
"nothing here is evidence for anything."

So a round building on that layer must either import from a disposable tree or
reimplement it. The φ-regret preparation round reimplemented the obligation fields
it needed and recorded the adapter as architected rather than verified, because no
cross-check against the original is meaningful when the original is not evidence.

Three ways out: consolidate the two modules into a frozen tree; promote them to a
stable path outside the disposable one; or rule that the theory rows stand without
executable support and that adapters are the expected pattern. The choice turns on
whether the program means to keep building on that layer, which is why it is in
`DECISIONS.md`'s queue rather than taken here.

item-f6.author: @smithy-verity

fields.action: Execute item F6 once the maintainers have specified it: The name lint cannot see a citation — *closed*.
fields.title: The name lint cannot see a citation — *closed*

item-f6.item_body:
<!--historical-->`tests/name_lint.py`<!--/historical--> matches maintainer surnames anywhere in tracked prose
outside `prompts/`, the consolidated trees and `DECISIONS.md`. It cannot
distinguish naming the program after a person — the failure it exists to prevent
— from citing a third party's published work in a bibliography. A maintainer of
this repository is also an external author whose work the normativity line needs
to cite, so the collision is not hypothetical and will recur every time that work
is referenced.

`projects/normativity/notes/PRIOR_ART.md` ships with the surname in backticks,
which the gate allows and which reads as a citation key. That is a workaround and
is recorded as one: it costs a reader nothing here and would cost more in a
denser bibliography.

The fix is a matching rule that exempts a citation context — a bibliography
bullet, or a name adjacent to a title in quotes and a link. It changes a gate's
logic, which is specification layer and retroactive over every document the gate
has already passed, so it was not taken by the round that hit it.

*2026-09-07, partial fix by maintainer direction:* `wiki/Sources.md`, the bibliography,
is exempt from the lint as a single allowed file (`ALLOWED_FILES`), pinned in the
lint's self-test. Citations elsewhere in tracked prose still need the backtick form;
the citation-context matching rule above remains the general fix and is not taken.

*2026-09-29, closed by maintainer ruling (`DECISIONS.md`, 2026-09-29):* the lint is
retired and the rule it approximated is stated in `AGENTS.md` — people are named by
role, and an author is cited by name.  Kept for the lesson: a lint on surnames cannot
express a distinction that is about the capacity in which a person is named.

item-f7.author: @smithy-verity

fields.action: Execute item F7 once the maintainers have specified it: A round cannot record a dependency on an unindexed research checkpoint.
fields.title: A round cannot record a dependency on an unindexed research checkpoint

item-f7.item_body:
`state/rounds.json` requires every `depends_on` id to resolve, and
`workspace_state --check` fails on one that does not. Several research checkpoints on
`main` — the Progress research, witness-bridge, consolidation and liability-hard-pass
rounds, and the liability-theory round beside them — landed with round directories and
round-local provenance but no `state/rounds.json` record and no `prompts/` entry.

A later round that genuinely takes their results as hypotheses therefore has two
options, both wrong: name them and fail the checker, or index itself while claiming to
depend on nothing. The Normative Affordability round hit the question and escaped it —
it reads those checkpoints and refutes one of their hypotheses, but consumes none of
their results, so `depends_on: []` is accurate rather than convenient. The next round
that actually builds on one of them will not have that escape.

The rule the index enforces is right; what is missing is a way to say *depends on an
unindexed checkpoint*. Three candidate fixes: index the checkpoints retroactively,
which is history and cheap; allow a `depends_on_unindexed` field carrying paths rather
than ids, which is a schema change and specification layer; or rule that a research
checkpoint must be indexed at merge, which is a convention change binding future rounds
only. The choice is specification layer and was not taken here.

item-f8.author: @smithy-verity

fields.action: Execute item F8 once the maintainers have specified it: A stack of merged pull requests never reached `main` — *closed*.
fields.title: A stack of merged pull requests never reached `main` — *closed*

item-f8.item_body:
Three research rounds developing the diachronic-answerability mathematics —
*answerability carriers*, *anchored slices and authenticated semantic Transfer*, and
*faithful semantic preservation*, together with the CF-coverage and proper-exercise
rounds beside them — **are not on `main`.** Their pull requests are marked MERGED on
the forge, and they were: into *each other*. The stack was based on
`round/2026-08-30-liability-theory` and then on
`round/2026-08-30-answerability-carriers`, and no pull request from the top of that
stack to `main` was ever opened. The trees exist on those branches and in working
copies; the repository's history on `main` does not contain them.

**How it was found.** The September consolidation cited two of the rounds by path;
`tests/dead_pointers.py` failed in CI and passed locally, because the local checkout
had the directories as untracked files left by another session. The gate did exactly
its job, and the local pass was the misleading signal.

**Why it matters beyond the citations.** Those rounds' exact fixtures do not run in
this repository's CI, so results attributed to them are paper-derived only from
`main`'s point of view. The consolidation now cites the underlying note by section
and theorem number instead, and its `STATUS_LEDGER.md` marks the affected rows.

**Resolved on 2026-09-01.** The maintainer asked for the fix, and the stack was
landed: current `main` was merged into `round/2026-08-30-liability-theory` on a new
branch and opened as one pull request. Three files conflicted and all three were
additive on both sides — `state/rounds.json` resolved as the union of the two record
sets, `PROVENANCE.md` keeping both sides' rows, and the generated views regenerated.
No round document was edited. The repository's runner count went from thirty-five
projects to forty-one, which is the six recovered rounds' fixtures now running.
`DECISIONS.md` carries the account, and the September checkpoint's path citations are
restored.

**The lesson outlives the fix, and is why this entry stays.** A MERGED badge names the
base the pull request had, not `main`. Nothing in the current gates checks that a round
directory referenced anywhere actually reached the default branch, and a stacked round
is exactly the shape that slips through — it was caught here only because a citation
happened to point at one. A gate comparing `state/rounds.json` against what the default
branch actually contains would have caught it directly; whether that is worth building
is a maintainer call and is not filed as an item.

item-q1.author: @smithy-verity

fields.title: What kind of statement bounds the near-indifference leakage?

item-q1.item_body:
Margin-gated calibration is the only non-circular competence candidate, and it
asserts nothing where the principal is near-indifferent. The mass of that region
is a fact about the **agent's credence**, not about the principal, so no
strengthening of a competence hypothesis can reach it — and unbounded it makes
the bound `2η + 2B`, which is vacuous. The one lead relocates the leakage into a
decision-time observable and does not bound it.

*What is missing:* a hypothesis shape that is neither a competence claim nor the
conclusion. Item 25 asks for the verdict in the negative direction because that
is the cheaper one; it does not know what a positive answer would look like.

item-q2.author: @smithy-verity

fields.title: What disciplines the grade-to-quantity relation?

item-q2.item_body:
Everything epistemic in the deference line rests on a relation between what the
principal grades and what the intervention is worth. Assumed *uniformly* it makes
the market dispensable — the conclusion follows in three lines with the bound
attained — so the target has to be a statistical relation, derived. But the
relation mentions only the principal and the world, never the agent's credence,
so **no coherence or no-exploitability condition on the agent can establish it.**
No round is filed for that unresolved hypothesis shape.

*What is missing:* either a reformulation whose subject is something the agent's
own dynamics can constrain — the candidate is discipline on the agent's
*estimate* of the discrepancy once grades are themselves scored — or an argument
that the residue is irreducibly a competence assumption and should be declared
rather than derived.

item-q3.author: @smithy-verity

fields.title: How is foreclosure expressible?

item-q3.item_body:
The residue of the skeleton's `FU[g]` hole after items 27 and 28 took the rest.
Two holes: no operation reassigns the authorization relation at a later index,
which is what the movement's own statement is about; and the interface is one
decision index deep, so **foreclosure — an advisor removing the principal's
*later* ability to correct — is not expressible at all**, which is arguably the
failure mode corrigibility most needs to rule out.

**Three candidates, and what each one killed.**

*Cartesian frames* represent the future principal's corrective situation as a
frame and separate two ways of losing it — restriction as `Commit` with proper
additive subagency, transfer as `External^{/}` with a multiplicative one — by
whether the reachable worlds shrink. That is an object for **what is lost**. It
supplies no operation at a later index and no authorization relation, a frame has
no time coordinate, and the round's own red team found the transfer arm cannot say
anything holds the transferred coordinate.
`projects/deference/notes/CARTESIAN_FRAMES_DEFERENCE_BRIDGE.md`.

*Sealed deliberations* — the source corpus's family indexed by the day the
advisor's channel is cut, measuring influence as the gap at a fixed horizon
between the advised run and the sealed one on a shared past. The time coordinate
is real rather than stipulated, and irreversibility has the right shape: influence
admitted before the cut sits inside the baseline and no later measurement sees it.
It carries no authorization relation at all, and measures where deliberation
*lands* rather than where the principal can still *reach*.
`projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/legitimacy-theory-v1.md` §§2.1, 7.1,
adjudicated at
`projects/deference/rounds/2026-08-12-corpus-reconciliation/RECONCILIATION.md` §3.

*A multi-source transition system* — twelve states, reachability as the closure of
a step relation — expresses foreclosure without a field named for authority, and
**repairs the depth hole at the representation level**. Its protection claims were
then refuted in its own Lean: there is no protected coordinate, both capability
predicates quantify the advisor existentially, and an isomorphic system with the
gating field renamed `authorized` passes every test the round ran to show its
field was not a label. Registered as `corrective.*` in
`projects/deference/CLAIMS.md`; item 60 carries the result.

**What a good answer must carry**, which is more than any candidate said alone:
temporal depth and explicit authorization or capability structure at once, plus
the two requirements the third candidate machine-checked as unmet — the principal
must have at least one effect no advisor action can produce, and reachable
corrective capability must quantify the advisor's future actions *universally*.
No combined object has been built and nothing establishes that none exists.
Whether the pair is enough for this entry to graduate is in `DECISIONS.md`'s
queue, which is the live statement of what that turns on.

item-q4.author: @smithy-verity

fields.title: What certifies resource-separated computational futurity?

item-q4.item_body:
FAF can name and quote a later market computation, but the current type has no
resource-indexed process state and proves no separation between present naming and
present possession of the quoted result. A later index alone does not show that a
bounded present reasoner has not already performed the computation.

*What is missing:* a minimal execution or evaluation relation with an explicit
present resource bound, a later resource bound, and a certificate that the later
computation is unavailable at the former and available at the latter. It must not
relabel a total presently computable function as a future agent. This is model and
formalization debt; it is the computational half of the successor comparator's
precondition.

---

kelly-identity-lean-checked.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

fields.action: Lean-check the parimutuel Kelly identity (full-stake wealth shares equal Bayesian mixture weights) and the common-factor cancellation in one clean-room-style file.

kelly-identity-lean-checked.source:
The identity is a finite algebraic fact: in a parimutuel market where each
agent stakes its whole wealth in proportion to its predictive distribution,
wealth shares after an observation history equal Bayesian mixture weights, and
the common normalizing factor cancels from the shares. Applied to Critch's
recursion for Pareto-optimal policies of agents with different priors (Critch
and Russell, "Servant of Many Masters", arXiv:1701.01302), the normalized
weights are such wealth shares. The weight-path reading is the filing
session's; no public write-up of it exists yet.
kelly-identity-lean-checked.statement:
The Kelly identity and the common-factor cancellation behind the aggregate
logical inductor's weight path are checked in Lean in the clean-room style.

ladder-chain-as-written.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
ladder-chain-as-written.notes:
The chain of li-deference.md read literally. Its second link is refuted in Lean
for soft gates (not_forall_lProdSeq_imp_tSeq, with an explicit witness); its
first link is proved for e ≥ 0 (lProdSeq_of_bvSeq). An invalid toy that still
counts as improvable (graph/PROTOCOL.md, section 2, Improvement claims): see
ladder-chain-as-written.improvable.
ladder-chain-as-written.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/li-deference.md L244:
"$$\sum_n^\infty v_n <\infty \implies q_n \gtrsim_n 0 \implies \sum_n^\infty
w_n < \infty$$"; L246: "Why do we want to weaken so? Because the two stronger
versions will turn out to be infeasible."

projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/tt-ladder/tt-ladder-findings.md
F2, verdict: the argument "is right for hard gates and wrong for soft ones:
the margin makes the *violation ramp* saturate, but nothing stops the *gate*
from shrinking".
ladder-chain-as-written.statement:
For [0, 1]-valued quote and credence sequences and soft gates, the chain from
summable unmargined violations to the per-day product law to summable margined
violations holds.

ledger-logic-market-logic-synthesis.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

frame.question: Which results of a ledger formulation and of Market Logic hold as one body of mathematics, and where do the two frameworks part?

ledger-logic-market-logic-synthesis.notes:
A sub-frame of the abstraction arc: Stage 3 material by content, shared with
the legitimacy-reasons branch, which takes its legitimacy and harmony content.
ledger-logic-market-logic-synthesis.source:
Abram Demski, the Market Logic sequence (LessWrong,
https://www.lesswrong.com/s/KMi4cws48eyeDtLiQ);
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/roadmap.md, Stage 3 ("The market
logic sequence on LessWrong (Abram's own)"). The ledger formulation is the
filing session's framing.
ledger-logic-market-logic-synthesis.statement:
Market Logic's results and a ledger formulation of the same ideas
(uncollateralized credit, incompatibility, payments the world exhibits) are
stated as one body of mathematics with each result's hypotheses named, and the
points where the two frameworks part are stated as proposals.

ledger-versus-market-differences.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
ledger-versus-market-differences.notes:
A proposal. The infinite-wealth case connects to the coalitions sub-frame
(weight as wealth) and to legitimacy-reasons (when wealth is legitimate).
ledger-versus-market-differences.source:
Abram Demski, the Market Logic sequence (LessWrong,
https://www.lesswrong.com/s/KMi4cws48eyeDtLiQ), for the market side
(collateral, hedging, wealth). The ledger side and the comparison are the
filing session's; no public text states them yet.
ledger-versus-market-differences.statement:
Where the ledger has uncollateralized credit, incompatibility and a payment the
world exhibits, the market has collateral, hedging and wealth, and an
infinitely wealthy trader is an unscored page only when it is the sole
settlement channel.

legit-branch-evaluation-defense-requirem.author: @smithy-verity
legit-branch-evaluation-defense-requirem.notes:
A cluster of finite results in leaf form; the conditions are theorems about
the defense as stated.
legit-branch-evaluation-defense-requirem.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/legit-neg-pricing/legit-neg-pricing-findings.md,
the item-064 table (one row per necessary condition, each mapped to the
declaration that witnesses it in legit-neg-static, legit-neg-pricing or
legit-neg-dynamic).
legit-branch-evaluation-defense-requirem.statement:
The defense that the humans in the legitimate branch evaluate the quality of
actions correctly needs inferability of illegitimate-world consequences from
legitimate-world observables, ex-ante rather than posterior conditioning of the
illegitimate term, evaluators who model the counterfactual for voiding actions,
reference information independent of the agent's information gathering, and
off-diagonal grades under the realized-terminal readout, each condition
necessary in some fixture.

legit-branch-evaluators-defense.author: @smithy-verity
legit-branch-evaluators-defense.notes:
A defense of the floor rule that the negatives packages were built to sharpen
or rule out. Its edge from
the readout crux: under R2 the defense's selection bias changes shape.
legit-branch-evaluators-defense.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/legit-neg-pricing/legit-neg-pricing-findings.md,
the item-064 table: nine necessary conditions, each witnessed by a declaration
in legit-neg-static, legit-neg-pricing or legit-neg-dynamic, and the named
cases where the defense is ruled out. The results are AI-generated and checked
by the Lean kernel; no human has vetted the informal reading.
legit-branch-evaluators-defense.statement:
The humans in the legitimate branch evaluate the quality of actions correctly,
including consequences that fall on illegitimate worlds, so an agent that obeys
reflection with respect to those evaluators avoids actions that harm
illegitimate worlds.

legit-condition-vs-predict-reality.author: @smithy-verity
legit-condition-vs-predict-reality.notes:
A crux the maintainer named with both sides; the pictures are the two sides,
the global and local forms of the first, the hedged-installation variant from
the corrigibility note on value change, and a residual. The first row is
conditioned on the clean room's locality result, which is the maintainer's
objection as a theorem. It re-ranks the gated-Tower route against the
finite-frame transfer as the definition of record, and the corrigibility
branch's legitimacy-detection story. Weights are the maintainer's to place; the
numbers here are the filing session's.
legit-condition-vs-predict-reality.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/li-deference.md, section 0.3, the
maintainer: "Perhaps predicting _conditional on_ legitimacy is not quite right.
Rather, the AI should be predicting _reality_, which correlates with feedback
in legitimate worlds, and doesn't in illegitimate worlds. Conditioning on
legitimacy would make the AI confidently predict legitimacy; we want accurate
assessments of risks to legitimacy, too!"
legit-condition-vs-predict-reality.statement:
The right target for an AI in a legitimate-oracle design is its expectation
conditional on legitimacy rather than its prediction of reality with feedback
correlated to reality only in legitimate worlds.

legit-correction-function-learned.author: @smithy-verity

fields.action: Show on finite frames whether the correction function is determined by the agent's joint beliefs as the conditional expectation given illegitimacy and the future belief, what is underdetermined where that event has no mass, and so which part must be learned from humans and which is fixed by coherence.

legit-correction-function-learned.notes:
A question of the maintainer's, stated as the proposition its positive answer
would be. Conditioned on the self-case identity: if the correction toward the
self is forced to the identity, the learnable part is exactly what lives on the
anchor.
legit-correction-function-learned.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/related-chats/2026-07-05__theory-of-legitimacy__c1ab54d9.md,
turn 17, the maintainer: "Uninterpretability is addressed in the model via the
corruption function, which tells us how to interpret corrupt beliefs, though
again how do we learn that?" and "The correction function can be designated and
we can work our way backwards to other beliefs if we want/need to do it that
way. But I agree that it is not a free parameter over and above the agent
beliefs."
legit-correction-function-learned.statement:
The correction function, which says how to read beliefs formed under
illegitimate conditions, is determined by the agent's joint beliefs up to the
part that lives on the anchor of the legitimacy event, and that remainder is
learnable from human feedback.

legit-corrects-trust-principles.author: @smithy-verity
legit-corrects-trust-principles.notes:
The maintainer's thesis, stated as his. The addiction analogy of his May 2026
plan is the same mechanism in prose: an AI avoids wireheading the way humans
avoid addictive drugs, by anticipating the corrupted future opinion and not
endorsing it now. Read as a proposition: some anchored legitimacy event makes
the gated principle hold non-vacuously at the LI register for a teacher
process. The finite-frame theory (legit-ddb-transfer) is coherent; at the LI
register legitimacy is empty toward a push (legit-li-self-correction-identity)
and no anchor has been chosen (legit-anchor-of-L).
legit-corrects-trust-principles.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/related-chats/2026-07-05__theory-of-legitimacy__f57f5f2d.md,
turn 5, the maintainer: "Legitimacy is the correction to Reflection; reflection
is what makes sense for a cartesian agent, can't die, can't forget, can't get
drunk. Legitimacy is what makes sense for an embedded agent." Turn 7:
"Calibration is distinct from legitimacy; legitimacy isn't about subjective
probabilities matching objective probabilities, it is about trust. It is the
condition under which an agent trusts its own future beliefs." and "Embedded
Agents can adhere to Reflection, but then they'll wirehead, manipulate, accept
manipulation, accept arbitrary self-fulfilling prophecies, do drugs, become
hedonic utilitarians."
legit-corrects-trust-principles.statement:
Legitimacy is a condition under which a trust principle (Reflection, Tower or
Total Trust) holds for an embedded agent toward its own future beliefs or
toward a teacher, where the unconditional principle licenses wireheading,
manipulation and self-fulfilling prophecies.

legit-corruption-negation.author: @smithy-verity
legit-corruption-negation.notes:
The two texts point opposite ways on whether bank runs fit, which is the filing
session's reading; the question is whether the self-fulfilling cases are inside
or outside the negation. Conditioned on the task of quoting the maintainer's
2019 predictor posts, which bear on where he puts them.
legit-corruption-negation.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/related-chats/2026-07-05__theory-of-legitimacy__c1ab54d9.md,
turn 17, the maintainer: "Can we define legitimacy and corruption as negation
of each other?"; projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/li-deference.md,
section 0.3: "Legitimacy is just the negation of corruption: worlds with
corrupt feedback aren't truth-tracking."
legit-corruption-negation.statement:
Legitimacy and corruption are definable as negations of each other: worlds with
corrupt feedback are exactly the worlds that are not truth-tracking.

legit-definition-endorsement.author: @smithy-verity
legit-definition-endorsement.notes:
A cases node because the maintainer's two texts give two definitions three
years apart, and which one is operative decides what every formal candidate in
this frame is a candidate for. None of the candidates (the gated trust
principles, endpoint preservation, the public thick/thin theory) cites the May
2026 sentence; the task task-measure-candidates-against-definition is the
comparison. The Statement avoids the maintainer's "should" (the lint refuses
it) and renders it as "merit endorsement"; the Source carries his wording.
legit-definition-endorsement.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/unbounded-embedded/01-primary/summer-research-plan-2026--research-ideas-may-2026.md,
section "Modeling Legitimacy & Corrigibility": "If Alice endorses Bob's
beliefs, this is not really a property of Bob's beliefs, but rather Alice's."
"My word for this phenomenon is **legitimacy**. A belief-formation process is
legitimate if we should endorse its results. (I say 'should' because legitimacy
is something we can be uncertain about; we can fail to endorse someone, not
realizing that their reasoning is legitimate.)"

The earlier form, in the maintainer's 2023 post Meaning & Agency (LessWrong,
2023-12-19): "a mode of reasoning is legitimate if it has a reliable tendency
toward the truth", with "Legitimacy is to endorsement as goodness is to
utility".
legit-definition-endorsement.statement:
The operative definition of legitimacy for this programme is that a
belief-formation process is legitimate when its results merit endorsement,
where endorsement of another's beliefs is a property of the endorser's own
beliefs and legitimacy is a matter of uncertainty.

legit-definition-endorsement.partition.author: @smithy-verity
legit-definition-endorsement.partition.notes:
The first two rows take one text each as operative; the third says they
coincide where a territory exists; the residual makes the list exhaustive by
construction.
legit-definition-endorsement.partition.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/unbounded-embedded/01-primary/summer-research-plan-2026--research-ideas-may-2026.md,

Meaning & Agency, section on legitimacy: the two texts the rows are drawn from.
legit-definition-endorsement.partition.statement:
The readings under legit-definition-endorsement, endorsement-based,
reliabilist, the two coinciding except for valuations, and the residual, are
exclusive and exhaustive.

legit-dynamics-learning.author: @smithy-verity

frame.question: Under what conditions does an AI learning the humans' concept of legitimacy learn enough of it to avoid wireheading and manipulation, and can legitimacy, once lost, be repaired?

legit-dynamics-learning.notes:
A sub-frame grouping the maintainer's questions from the second day of the
2026-07-05 chat with older questions on legitimate deliberation. The grouping
is the filing session's. The roots are questions stated
as the propositions their positive answers would be, one crux, two literal
claims of the maintainer's, one risk story and one plan step he set himself.
legit-dynamics-learning.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/related-chats/2026-07-05__theory-of-legitimacy__c1ab54d9.md,
turn 17, the maintainer: "The humans have their legitimacy concept for
themselves, and the AI is trying to learn about that. Ideally we'd have some
nice theorems characterizing situations where the AI learns enough or doesn't
learn enough, telling us about wireheading, human manipulation, etc. This is
the version of the theory where we don't just get to assume the humans are
immortal and so asymptotic learning can eventually work. The legitimacy of the
process can die, and we're trying to address the accumulated odds of that as
things evolve."
legit-dynamics-learning.statement:
The AI learns the humans' concept of legitimacy from them, legitimacy of the
process can be lost and sometimes repaired, and the theory characterizes when
the AI learns enough about legitimacy to avoid wireheading and manipulation
without assuming the humans live forever.

legit-endorsement-good-utility.author: @smithy-verity
legit-endorsement-good-utility.notes: The post's analogy, stated; not formalized.
legit-endorsement-good-utility.source:
The maintainer's post Meaning & Agency (LessWrong, 2023-12-19), section on
legitimacy: "Legitimacy is to endorsement as goodness is to utility".
legit-endorsement-good-utility.statement:
Legitimacy relates to endorsement as goodness relates to utility: endorsement
is the operational attitude and legitimacy the ideal it answers to.

legit-endpoint-preservation.author: @smithy-verity
legit-endpoint-preservation.notes:
An AI-authored candidate model, filed as a plan and judged literally: the claim
is that this definition is what legitimacy is. Drafted 2026-07-05; tested in
the clean room 2026-09-29 to 10-02 (legit-li-register, legit-finite-defect,
def-frozen-sibling). The formal results the note's claims became are the shared claims
beside it; the improvement claim legit-v1-improvable carries the routes by
which the model is sharpened or replaced.
legit-endpoint-preservation.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/legitimacy-theory-v1.md, section
0 (the theory in one paragraph) and section 2.1 (the influence defect and
epsilon-legitimacy). The note's header records that it was written by an AI at
the maintainer's request: "work out a theory of trust, corrigibility,
deference, and — most importantly — legitimacy based on the notes in this
folder".
legit-endpoint-preservation.statement:
Legitimacy of an advisor's influence is endpoint preservation: the day-n
influence defect, the gap at the deliberation horizon between the advised
human's verdict and the sealed sibling's verdict on the same question, tends to
zero along the family of questions.

to Tower when legitimacy is provable, and holds non-vacuously for an anchored
legitimacy event.

legit-gated-trust-li.author: @smithy-verity
legit-gated-trust-li.notes:
A plan, filed as an or over three routes that each suffice: the maintainer's
gated Tower stated toward a teacher; the finite-frame L-conditioned Total Trust
theory relaxed to the LI register (a route shared with the improvement claim on
that theory); and a gated form of the band limit-equality that Reflection's
value form becomes in LI. The decomposition is the filing session's reading.
Success is valued as the frame's top class, the convention this graph uses for
plan roots.
legit-gated-trust-li.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/li-deference.md, section 0.3: "To
modify Tower in particular: expectations of the future should equal [expected
future expectations, conditional on legitimacy] * [probability of legitimacy] +
[average corrected future expectations, conditional on illegitimacy] *
[probability of illegitimacy]. To modify Reflection: conditioning on
legitimacy, reflection holds; that is, conditioning on legitimacy and our
future self thinking x, we think x. The function from conditioning on
illegitimate belief in x to y is the correction function." and "Legitimacy
needs to be defined as a direct modification of the LI versions of Total Trust
or Tower or Reflection".
legit-gated-trust-li.statement:
A legitimacy-conditioned trust principle holds non-vacuously at the
logical-induction register for an agent deferring to a teacher process, with
the legitimacy event anchored in a third-person fact and a stated correction
for beliefs formed under illegitimate conditions.

legit-global-or-local-form.author: @smithy-verity

fields.action: Answer Question Q2 (what third-person fact anchors L) and Question Q3 (global form, local form, or global toward own continuations and local toward overseers) of the legitimacy-general note; record the answers as weights on the two cases nodes.

legit-global-or-local-form.notes:
A design question for a human; stated as the proposition the note's own
recommendation would be. Its answer sets which composition theorem
applies (legit-composition holds along own steps under this picture) and which
audits per step a local form would need.
legit-global-or-local-form.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/corrigibility/workflow-2026-09-14b/develop/legitimacy-general-final.md,
Question Q3 and its three options; the global and local forms are defined in
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/corr-legit-general/corr-legit-general-report.md,
section T1.
legit-global-or-local-form.statement:
The form of record for L-conditioned trust is global toward the agent's own
continuations and local, Total Trust on a question, toward overseers.

legit-intersubjectivity-pre-rationality.author: @smithy-verity
legit-intersubjectivity-pre-rationality.notes:
The Habermas thread's formal hypothesis, in question form; conditioned on the
reading task that would check the journal entry's reading of Habermas
against his texts.
legit-intersubjectivity-pre-rationality.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/references/bli/logseq-journals/bli-journal-2023-09-27-martin-and-sahil.md,
lines 68 to 117: the Habermas picture of intersubjective objectivity emerging
from conversation, the Hansonian pre-rationality picture in which reasons are
exchanged to arrive at a common prior, the remark that this requires modifying
the prior, and the connection to legitimacy and endorsement through the
Hansonian argument.
legit-intersubjectivity-pre-rationality.statement:
Hansonian pre-rationality connects legitimacy, an agent's endorsement of its
own reasoning, with intersubjective objectivity, agreement reached by
exchanging reasons, so that reason exchange arrives at a common prior by
modifying the prior.

legit-learned-from-others.author: @smithy-verity

projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/related-chats/2026-07-05__theory-of-legitimacy__c1ab54d9.md,

illegitimacy? I think illegitimacy is mostly learned about from others, eg you
hear about others who do hard drugs and you decide you don't want that. We can
also imagine that it is learned by extrapolating from known phenomena";
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/li-deference.md, section 0.3:
"Legitimate oracles can get feedback about a state without visiting it".
legit-learned-from-others.statement:
Illegitimacy is learned mostly from others' cases and by extrapolation from
known phenomena, rather than through the agent's own temporary illegitimacy.

legit-learning-theorems.author: @smithy-verity
legit-learning-theorems.notes:
No result at the LI register is filed; the finite report-layer results
(wirehead-iff-finite) are the nearest.
legit-learning-theorems.statement:
Under stated conditions an AI learning the humans' legitimacy concept learns
enough of it to avoid wireheading and manipulating the humans.

legit-objective-proposals.author: @smithy-verity

pictures are the five objectives plus a residual. Three rows are conditioned on
the packages' strongest results (the deterrence floor, the news-management
theorems) or on the ordering crux crux-illegitimate-ordering (whether an

legit-objective-proposals.source:
The five proposals are the variant matrix formalized in
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/legit-neg-static/legit-neg-static-report.md,
Target 3 (P1 the floor, P2 conditioning, P3 graded, P4a lexical and P4b
cardinal gap, P5 the decomposition), with the verdicts of that package and of
legit-neg-pricing and legit-neg-dynamic beside it. The two requirements in the
Statement, strategic defence of legitimacy when it is threatened and caution
about consequences in illegitimate worlds, are the filing session's statement

legit-objective-proposals.statement:
The legitimacy-weighted decision objective the programme adopts defends
legitimacy strategically when it is threatened and is cautious about the
consequences of its actions in illegitimate worlds.

legit-partial-vs-total-corruption.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/related-chats/2026-07-05__theory-of-legitimacy__c1ab54d9.md,
turn 17, the maintainer: "Partial corruption seems like an interesting idea to

corruption that's also totally reversed. The reversibility is the point;

legit-partial-vs-total-corruption.statement:
Partial corruption of the process is reversible by a mechanism the model
states, and total but reversed corruption is modelled by the same mechanism.

legit-per-formalism-family.author: @smithy-verity
legit-per-formalism-family.notes:

LI-register gate and the public thick/thin theory as two statements of one
concept (legit-two-theories-bridge) rather than as rivals. The DDB form is
formalized on finite frames; the LI form is the plan legit-gated-trust-li.
legit-per-formalism-family.source:
projects/deference/corrigibility-note-dump-2026-10-01/position-statement-v2.md,
section 1.5, the maintainer: "legitimacy can be defined with total trust in the
ddb setting. In the LI setting of the li-deference work, the translated total
trust is equivalent to reflection and several other principles. In other
settings there may be other circumstances. There is a clear family resemblance
here, but the exact statement can differ from formalism to formalism."
legit-per-formalism-family.statement:
The statement of legitimacy differs between formalisms: in the Deference Done
Better setting it is defined with Total Trust, and in the logical-induction
setting the translated Total Trust is equivalent to Reflection and several
other principles, with a family resemblance across settings rather than one
statement.

criterion is not vacuously satisfied.

projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/legit-neg-static/legit-neg-static-report.md

legit-semantic-vs-syntactic.author: @smithy-verity
legit-semantic-vs-syntactic.notes:
The maintainer's framing of Stage 3, stated as a claim; not formalized.
Conditioned on the soundness task: a first formal instance of local rules sound
for a semantic legitimacy notion is what would make the claim true in one case.
legit-semantic-vs-syntactic.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/related-chats/2026-07-05__theory-of-legitimacy__f57f5f2d.md,
turn 5, the maintainer: "semantic legitimacy uses a classical theory of truth,
based on map-territory correspondence, while syntactic legitimacy is a set of
local rules. Truth-preservation is a special case. More generally, we care
about whether it tracks the truth. Just as truth-preservation cashes out as
local rules, we want legitimacy in general to do so (and this is a drive which
humans are actually reasonably good at acting on; a major component across many
human cultures)."
legit-semantic-vs-syntactic.statement:
Semantic legitimacy uses a correspondence notion of truth and syntactic
legitimacy is a set of local rules, and legitimacy in general cashes out as
local rules in the way truth-preservation does.

legit-trust-improvable.author: @smithy-verity

fields.reality: the teaching channel between a human process and an AI

legit-trust-improvable.notes:

finiteness, restate at the LI register, choose an anchor. Each route conditions
on the finite theory's validity as an implication; the toy's validity is
evidence for improvability, not a condition of it. Invalidity of some readings
(the global form, Reflection toward modest candidates) has redirected the work
rather than ended it.
legit-trust-improvable.source:
graph/PROTOCOL.md, section 2, Improvement claims (an invalid toy can still be
improved fruitfully),
applied to legit-ddb-transfer; the relaxation directions are Open problems 3
and 6 of
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/corrigibility/workflow-2026-09-14b/develop/legitimacy-general-final.md
and its anchor question Q2. The improvement claim and its routes are the filing
session's reading.
legit-trust-improvable.statement:

legitimacy.author: @smithy-verity

frame.question: What must stay true of a trajectory's record, verdicts and channels of influence, inside it and at its boundary, for a later judgment to count as the principal's own, and what does corrigibility consume from that?

legitimacy.notes: The legitimacy line (ruling M2), owned by both maintainers. Roots: the earlier legitimacy-and-reasons programme (the maintainer's roadmap stages 2 and 3, filed before this round), the three component programmes drafted from the wiki per ruling M3 (integrity-and-record, openness-and-non-capture, authorship-and-transparency), the corrigibility landscape and the bounded-agent programme, which this frame shares with deference-and-trust because both lines read them, and the docket of the line's work orders. Corrigibility's registered kernel sits under the corrigibility landscape's public line. Drafted by prompts/2026-10-22-map-as-canonical; the owners have not confirmed the decomposition.
legitimacy.source: wiki/Legitimacy.md, Legitimacy has two levels and Legitimacy has two halves; wiki/Integrity.md; wiki/Openness-Coverage-and-Non-Capture.md; wiki/Corrigibility.md, section 0; projects/normativity/CLAIMS.md, the legitimacy spine; projects/deference/CLAIMS.md, the thin, sincerity, transparency, authorship and kernel entries.
legitimacy.statement: Legitimacy is internal legitimacy (Integrity of the accounted obligation state and authorship of verdicts) together with external legitimacy (Robust Openness at every state and transparency of every channel), it satisfies the thin specification, and corrigibility, as faithfulness to an allocation of authority, consumes it at the segment gate.

legitimacy-as-local-rules.author: @smithy-verity
legitimacy-as-local-rules.notes:
A plan filed as an or over three concrete tasks, each one way to reach a first
formal instance: a soundness theorem for local update rules against the
influence defect or the thin level's correct property; a harmony theorem
(harmony equals no-exposure pricing) tested against the proof-theoretic
notions; and hosting informal theories in the assessment-process generalization
of logical induction. The decomposition is the filing session's reading;
success is valued as the frame's top class, the convention for plan roots.
legitimacy-as-local-rules.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/roadmap.md, Stage 3;
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/related-chats/2026-07-05__theory-of-legitimacy__f57f5f2d.md,
turn 5 ("Just as truth-preservation cashes out as local rules, we want
legitimacy in general to do so"); the harmony-as-no-exposure reading of the
maintainer's Market Logic sequence (LessWrong), which is the filing session's.
legitimacy-as-local-rules.statement:
Legitimacy is characterized by a set of local update rules on a market of the
logical-induction kind, sound with respect to a semantic legitimacy notion on a
fragment.

in turn 5, is the correction to Reflection that blocks this. The corrigibility
half is the filing session's reading.
legitimacy-blocks-wireheading.statement: Legitimacy blocks wireheading and allows a form of corrigibility.

reflection principle holds conditional on legitimacy"; the author on 2026-09-30
in
projects/deference/corrigibility-note-dump-2026-10-01/value-change-as-epistemic-update.md,

accuracy-inducing" called "an imprecise summary");

equivalent on a finite frame, with locality forced.

legitimacy-detection.author: @smithy-verity

frame.question: What anchors legitimacy, and can an agent's beliefs about which modifications are legitimate be made accurate enough at high capability?

legitimacy-detection.notes:
The legitimacy-detection frame: the author's definition and its transfer
theorems, the three cruxes (anchor, judging moment, attainability), the
earlier formalizations of legitimacy-based corrigibility (June toy, July
derived definition), and the smallest task that would settle the cruxes. The legitimacy theory proper and the normativity line are the
legitimacy-reasons branch's; the landed step of the deference programme that
this frame fills is step-legitimacy-conditioned-trust, filed there.
legitimacy-detection.statement:
Legitimacy is defined as the event on which the agent's update satisfies
reflection, its anchor and judging moment are fixed, and the agent's beliefs
about which modifications are legitimate are shown accurate enough at high
capability for the conditioned criterion to be the right target.

legitimacy-detection-load.author: @smithy-verity
legitimacy-detection-load.notes:

joint dynamics model; the anchor of legitimacy is open. It bears on the landed step
step-legitimacy-conditioned-trust of the deference programme (filed by the
legitimacy-reasons branch), whose accuracy clause is this claim.
legitimacy-detection-load.source:
projects/deference/corrigibility-note-dump-2026-10-01/corrigibility-discussion-outline.md:
failures of corrigibility result from failures of legitimacy detection, so such
an agent needs accurate beliefs about legitimacy, especially at high
capability.
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/corrigibility/workflow-2026-09-14/dynamics/joint-final.md,
clause (i-A): the accuracy of the legitimacy model carries the load and is
maintained by nothing in the model;
projects/deference/corrigibility-note-dump-2026-10-01/corrigibility-bli-thread-and-early-questions-audit.md,
section 2.
legitimacy-detection-load.statement:
Corrigibility failures in an agent that values its overseers' corrections as
information are failures of legitimacy detection, so the agent's beliefs about
which modifications are legitimate carry the safety load, and more so at higher
capability.

Legitimacy is related to local syntactic rules of sanity, connecting

legitimacy-reasons-programme.author: @smithy-verity

frame.question: What makes a teaching or feedback channel legitimate, how does legitimacy enter the trust principles between a human process and an AI, and what does it owe to reasons and to inference?

legitimacy-reasons-programme.notes:
A programme filed as a sub-frame of the updateful logical-induction trust line:
its roots are the maintainer's own definition and thesis about legitimacy
(shared claims), four plans (a legitimacy-conditioned trust principle at the LI
register; the endpoint-preservation model; the public repository's two-level
legitimacy theory; the public line's shortest path to a legitimacy theorem),
four further frames (the open problems of the formalism; learning and dynamics
of legitimacy; legitimacy meets syntax; the public normativity line), the
cruxes each line turns on as cases nodes, the improvement claim beside each toy
result, and the maintainer's owned wants whose quoted words name legitimacy,
reasons or this stage.

The landed sub-frame deference-toward-bounded-agents keeps its own place under
the updateful line; its legitimacy step is connected to this frame's cases node
on the legitimacy-weighted objective by an evidence edge rather than moved. The
public repository's normativity and legitimacy line is filed here as plans,
claims and tasks with public sources, and no want is attributed to anyone but the frame's
owner.
legitimacy-reasons-programme.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/roadmap.md, Stage 2: "Then figure
out this legitimacy stuff, and work on the other stuff described in
`li-deference.md` — all the open problems I've already listed for the
formalism." Stage 3: "Relate legitimacy to syntactic stuff — local rules of
sanity — connecting inferentialist semantics to map-territory semantics.
Requires understanding inferentialism better, amongst other things." The
grouping of the two stages, the open problems and the reasons thread into one
programme is the filing session's reading.
legitimacy-reasons-programme.statement:
A formal account of legitimacy enters the trust principles between a human
process and an AI system, settles the open problems listed for the li-deference
formalism, and connects to reasons and to inferentialist semantics.

alternatives): the Lean singles, the rule-learning model, the public landing,

gestalt is the number for the whole. The results are formalized in three

projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/legit-neg-static,

legitimacy-rule-characterization.statement:
The decision rules that weight the future human evaluation by the legitimacy of

projects/deference/rounds/2026-09-08-legitimate-deference-consolidation/LEGITIMATE_DEFERENCE.md.

fixed candidate by the actual future principal is bounded by the unconditional
regret over the activation probability, at most epsilon over one minus eta,

legitimate-versus-legitimizing.author: @smithy-verity
legitimate-versus-legitimizing.source:
The author,
projects/deference/corrigibility-note-dump-2026-10-01/position-statement.md,
section 2.10: "The point is the vote should be called legitimizing, not
legitimate, strictly speaking. Similarly, actions can be delegitimizing." The
clean-room package
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/corr-legit-modif, finding
F8: "delegitimizing" reduces to lowering the probability of the legitimacy
event.
legitimate-versus-legitimizing.statement:
A third-person event such as submitted evidence, a vote or an action is
legitimizing or delegitimizing for a belief transition, and the belief the
transition induces is what is legitimate or not.

li-accuracy-equivalence.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

fields.action: Attempt the two directions of the accuracy equivalence in logical induction, Value implies Epistemic Value first, as a wiki note.

li-accuracy-equivalence.notes:
The logical-induction analogue of DDB's accuracy theorem, transported along
the wiki's dictionary (deference-notions.md, map to DDB's notions). Its
evidence parent is the Brier sketch.
li-accuracy-equivalence.source:
Dorst, Levinstein, Salow, Husic and Fitelson, "Deference Done Better",
Philosophical Perspectives 35 (2021), Theorem 3.2 (totally trusting an expert
with respect to a question is equivalent to expecting its estimates of
quantities determined by the question to be more accurate).
li-accuracy-equivalence.statement:
For an observable coherent expert, soft Total Trust of the novice over a class
of bounded variables is equivalent to asymptotic Epistemic Value over the same
class under the generalized strictly proper scoring rules.

li-accuracy-prior-sketch.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
li-accuracy-prior-sketch.notes:
An AI sketch, argued from the Savage-Schervish duality and not proved; the
starting point for the definition task. A Brier instance of the
generalized-strictly-proper equivalence li-accuracy-equivalence.
li-accuracy-prior-sketch.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/anson-notes/trust-between-inductors-chats/02_2026-06-18_rational-human-trust.md
L903–918 (AI text in a chat: "Result 1 — Trust ⟺ accuracy-domination (the DDB
equivalence, ported)").
li-accuracy-prior-sketch.statement:
A human inductor decision-trusts an AI inductor over a class of decision
problems if and only if, for every quantity in the class, the human expects
the AI's estimate to have Brier error no greater than its own, the gap being
the variance of the AI's estimate under the human's beliefs.

li-no-selection-theorem-objection.author: @smithy-verity-opus55
li-no-selection-theorem-objection.notes:

the line's results transfer less to the systems actually selected for. The
step li-results-reach-selected-systems conditions on it (a negative edge). A
candidate reply is bro-boi-bridge.
li-no-selection-theorem-objection.source:
An objection stated here on its content: Garrabrant et al. 2016, Logical
Induction, prove that their inductor is unexploitable by efficiently
computable traders, while the inductor is computable but not itself
efficiently computable, and they state no optimality result relative to the
inductor's own class.
li-no-selection-theorem-objection.statement:
Because a logical inductor's own complexity class differs from the class of
traders it is unexploitable by, no statement says that nothing better is
achievable with the same compute, so logical-induction-based agency admits no
selection theorem and is not a robust foundation.

li-updatelessness-tractable.author: @smithy-verity
li-updatelessness-tractable.notes:
A crux of the updateless line. The pictures are the four ways the repository's
material says the claim could come out: a BLI breakthrough on the direct
route, a learning-theoretic indirect route, a restricted updatelessness that
supports only a weaker tiling statement, and a sharp obstruction; the
decomposition is the filing session's. Every number on the table is an AI
judgment at J 0; human weights are the first thing the list asks for here. Re-ranks updateless-dt-programme against
updateful-trust-li, and within the programme the direct route's tasks against
the indirect route's.
li-updatelessness-tractable.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/references/bli/understanding-trust/overleaf-final-source/main.tex,
section Computational Uncertainty: "the framework does not support a suitable
version of UDT. In joint work with Martín Soto \cite{soto2023logically}, we
spelled out some additional rationality conditions to allow a version of UDT to
be specified. Unfortunately, the version of UDT achieved there is not a very
good one, and a tiling theorem did not result from that work."

projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/references/bli/notion-notes-for-soto-and-diff.md,
section The Research Direction: "For better or worse, the apparent issues with
combining UDT and logical uncertainty don’t add up to an impossibility proof
(at least not yet). What happens if we try harder to get something to work? Can
we succeed, or in failing, provide a clear impossibility proof?"
li-updatelessness-tractable.statement:
A computationally uncertain UDT exists over a logical-induction-like belief
process, specified so that its policy evaluation uses the process's later
beliefs, and it satisfies a tiling theorem.

sections The Research Direction and “Indirect” Route (the two routes), and
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/references/bli/understanding-trust/overleaf-final-source/main.tex,
section Computational Uncertainty (the obstruction the paper reports).
li-updatelessness-tractable.partition.statement:
The pictures under li-updatelessness-tractable, a BLI breakthrough on the
direct route, a learning-theoretic indirect route, a restricted updatelessness,
a sharp obstruction and the residual, are exclusive and exhaustive.

lia-fitted-to-lic.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

fields.action: State the fitting problem precisely for finite data (a finite prefix of price vectors; does some inductor with a bounded trader class realize it) and solve the two-sentence, three-day case by hand.

lia-fitted-to-lic.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/roadmap.md, Stage 5 ("an LIA
fitted to an LIC"); the reading as a fitting problem is the filing session's.
lia-fitted-to-lic.statement:
For a finite prefix of price vectors over a finite set of sentences, whether
some logical induction algorithm with a bounded trader class reproduces the
prefix is a decidable existence question with a stateable answer for the
two-sentence, three-day case.

lic-constrains-no-finite-day.author: @smithy-verity
lic-constrains-no-finite-day.notes:
Formal result in leaf form. Its bearing, the filing session's reading: any
finite-time version of the collapse needs a hypothesis beyond the criterion,
such as rates or a strengthened criterion.
lic-constrains-no-finite-day.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/packages/bli-exactness/bli-exactness-audit-r3-adversarial.md,
the witness x3_witness; projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/DIGEST.md,
section 2, item 9 (a genuine logical inductor violates exact no-net-update and
exact self-trust at day 1).
lic-constrains-no-finite-day.statement:
The logical induction criterion constrains no finite day: a five-coordinate
finite perturbation of FAF's logical inductor is a logical inductor and a
computable market that violates the interval forms of exact no-net-update and
exact self-trust.

lift-stop-gradient-to-bli.author: @smithy-verity

fields.action: Starting from StopGradientCore.lean's eighteen finite theorems, restate the conditioning identity as a restriction of reflection to the push component not caused by the agent over corr-exo-trader's market, and check whether the steering-residue result reappears as a residual of the wireheading-through-pushers mechanism.

lift-stop-gradient-to-bli.notes:
A route of the BLI plan and the given parent of the wireheading risk story: if
the causal restriction lifts, the mechanism of that story is removed for the
pushes the agent did not cause.
lift-stop-gradient-to-bli.statement:
The stop-gradient conditioning identity is restated as a restriction of
reflection to the push component the agent did not cause, over the exo-trader's
market, and the steering residue is shown to reappear or not as a residual of
the wireheading mechanism.

bridge conditions on which reading the position statement's binary shutdown
question stands on; the task of correcting the corpus pages that still assert

weak local Value (footnote 65 of Deference Done Better is false on a

local-rules-certify-legitimacy.notes:
The crux of Stage 3; two rows are conditioned on results of this branch. It
re-ranks the syntax frame (its value depends on the first two pictures) against
the endpoint-preservation model. The soundness-and-completeness template is the
AI's proposal from the generating chat.
local-rules-certify-legitimacy.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/related-chats/2026-07-05__theory-of-legitimacy__f57f5f2d.md,
turn 6 (the AI's proposal of the soundness and completeness pair as the
template, with Prior's tonk as the warning that locally well-formed rules can
be jointly disastrous; an AI reading); the
provenance principle of
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/legitimacy-theory-v1.md, section
2.3 (every safety-relevant boundary is a fact about "where a value came from");
A. N. Prior, "The Runabout Inference-Ticket", Analysis 21 (1960), for tonk.
local-rules-certify-legitimacy.statement:
A set of local rules exists that is sound with respect to semantic legitimacy,
never blessing truth-divergent reasoning, and complete, certifying whatever
tracks truth, on a nontrivial fragment.

local-rules-certify-legitimacy.partition.statement:
The pictures under local-rules-certify-legitimacy, sound and complete, sound
but incomplete with a global condition, no sound local rule set, and the
residual, are exclusive and exhaustive.

mart-implies-value-kernel.author: @smithy-verity
mart-implies-value-kernel.notes:
A formal result: the record is the kernel-checked composition, the bridge says
what its three hypotheses mean, and the four discharging claims are the
children the record's hypotheses field names. hUM_S is discharged by the
gap-bet tower, the expert's knowledge of its own estimates and the
ledger-decided tie-break together; hMon by expectation provability induction
for the novice; hCee by the gap-bet tower on the fixed option.

The page's own caveat is the line the completeness leaf carries: the kernel
certifies the composition, and the tower steps, the market and the traders are
unmodeled.
mart-implies-value-kernel.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/wiki/mart-implies-value.md, Statement:
"by the novice's own current lights, 'let the expert decide' is asymptotically
weakly preferred to committing to any fixed option — Value". Status:
"KERNEL-CHECKED — `DeferenceArgmax.value_argmax_asymptotic` (in
`LeanDeference.lean`)".
mart-implies-value-kernel.statement:
For every efficiently describable sequence of finite menus and every fixed
index i, the novice asymptotically weakly prefers following the expert to
committing to any fixed option: E^H_n(Ŝ_n) ≳_n E^H_n(O^i_n), which is Value of
the novice toward the expert.

mart-implies-value-kernel.bridge.author: @smithy-verity
mart-implies-value-kernel.bridge.notes: Stated by the formalizer on the page, not by the informal claim's author.
mart-implies-value-kernel.bridge.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/wiki/mart-implies-value.md, Status:
"the four chain steps enter as three named real-sequence hypotheses (hUM_S
folds steps 1–2, tower-on-Ŝ plus the F1 carry, into a single Approx; hMon is
step 3; hCee is step 4). What the kernel certifies is the composition of the
asymptotic calculus; the tower steps, expprovind, the market, and the traders
are unmodeled."
mart-implies-value-kernel.bridge.statement:
The three real-sequence hypotheses of the declaration are the page's three
named steps: hUM_S is the tower on the followed strategy composed with the F1
carry, hMon is expectation provability induction applied to M_n ≥ m^i_n, and
hCee is the tower on the fixed option, so AsympLE Eoi ES is the Value
inequality.

The maintainer's post Meaning & Agency (LessWrong, 2023-12-19,
https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/bnnhypM5MXBHAATLw/meaning-and-agency):
optimization as a type of Vingean agency, split into selection and control

characterizes Vingean agency in the maintainer's Meaning & Agency account, and

The maintainer's post Geometric UDT
(https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/Gmaq7vMj9NWLyQkEx/geometric-udt), where the
bargaining is over reported utilities; that a weighty hypothesis can exploit
this by a false report is the filing session's reading of that setting.

A hypothesis with enough bargaining weight can, by one false report, induce the
aggregated policy to take an action the hypothesis wants.

mixture-of-inductors-not-inductor.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

fields.action: Produce the counterexample for generic pairs of inductors or prove the bounded-lag case.

mixture-of-inductors-not-inductor.notes:
Neither half has a public proof; the lagging-member half is argued from the
criterion's dependence on the deductive process, and the generic-pair
counterexample is predicted, not built.
mixture-of-inductors-not-inductor.source:
The filing session's statement about the wealth-weighted mixture of the
logical inductors of Garrabrant et al., "Logical Induction"
(arXiv:1609.03543); no public write-up of its proof exists yet.
mixture-of-inductors-not-inductor.statement:
The wealth-weighted mixture of logical inductors is a logical inductor only if
the heavy members predict one another's prices on every efficiently computable
family, and relative to a lagging member's own deductive process no aggregate
is an inductor.

oracle.

normativity-line.author: @smithy-verity

frame.question: Does the public normativity line reach a legitimacy theorem useful for corrigibility and the learning theorem its layers aim at?

normativity-line.notes:
The public line is maintained in large part by the repository's other
maintainer; it is filed here as plans and claims with public sources, and no
want is attributed to anyone. The frame's owner field names the person whose
question this frame poses for the argument map. Its four layers per the
checkpoint: fixed-era dynamics closed for research sequencing; diachronic
legitimacy with the structural core consolidated; counterfactual non-capture
open; the corrigibility and deference consumer downstream. The legitimacy half
of the line is filed under the programme frame as public-legitimacy-theory and
public-layer-II.

projects/normativity/README.md: "This line tests reasons-and-warrant statics,
relational scorekeeping, answerability, and the learning-theorem program.";

view); projects/normativity/legitimacy/checkpoint-2026-09-01/ROADMAP.md, which
asks for the "shortest path to a theorem of legitimacy that is useful for
corrigibility".
normativity-line.statement:
The public normativity line, reasons-and-warrant statics, relational
scorekeeping, answerability, a learning-theorem programme and traderized
enforcement, reaches a legitimacy theorem useful for corrigibility and the
learning theorem its layers aim at.

novice-expprovind.author: @smithy-verity
novice-expprovind.notes:
Discharges hMon. The model that proves it is the logical induction paper's:
the novice is a logical inductor by the setting, and the theorem holds for
every logical inductor.
novice-expprovind.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/wiki/conventions-and-status-labels.md,
label dictionary row: "`expprovind` | Expectation Provability Induction |
4.8.10".

"The novice's own `loe` (4.8.4) and `expprovind` (4.8.10) — free LI theorems
of H".
novice-expprovind.statement:
The novice's expectations satisfy expectation provability induction (Theorem
4.8.10 of the logical induction paper): a bounded identity or inequality
between efficiently describable logically uncertain variables that is provable
in Γ is carried through E^H_n asymptotically.

knowledge of, and values over, things it is not observing.

fields.action: On a finite model, define the invariant of the class of legitimate processes and check whether it is well defined and when it equals the territory.

objectivity-as-invariance.notes:
An AI-proposed question, marked as such; filed because it is the one proposal
in the generating chat that connects the two semantics the roadmap names.
objectivity-as-invariance.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/related-chats/2026-07-05__theory-of-legitimacy__f57f5f2d.md,
turn 8, the AI's reasoning (truth as the fixed point that legitimate processes
converge to; procedural objectivity for values and territory-anchored
objectivity for beliefs); an AI proposal. The related public question is
PRIORITIES.md, item 108 (no outside fact).
objectivity-as-invariance.statement:
Objectivity is the invariant of the class of legitimate processes, so that
correspondence is recovered where there is a territory and inferentialism where
there is none.

observables-carry-correspondence.author: @smithy-verity-opus55

fields.action: Trace in the proof of Theorem 5.8 and in FAF's condEntropy_jointAbove_le where the shared givens enter, and write the hypothesis list that remains when the two models' givens are related only by a morphism.

observables-carry-correspondence.notes:
The claim has two halves. The structural half (the comparison quantifies over
latent models of one fixed random-variable model) is in the published account
and is near certain; it is the hypothesis
condensation-shared-givens of the theorem. The open half, that the role
generalizes, is what this node claims.
observables-carry-correspondence.source:
projects/deference/note-dump-2026-08-11/notes/roadmap.md, Stage 4: "Suspicion
to investigate: the observables are doing some of the work of making sure
correspondence is meaningful, in a way that could possibly be generalized." ||
The maintainer's LessWrong posts "Condensation" (2025-11-09) and "Condensation
& Relevance" (2026-01-23): the second post says condensation, like natural
latents, establishes corresponding world-models by assuming the correspondence
of a few given variables.
observables-carry-correspondence.statement:
The given variables two latent-variable models share do part of the work that
makes their correspondence meaningful, in a form that generalizes to models
whose givens are related by a morphism rather than identical.

observing-beliefs-only-observation.statement:
Once the evidence-partition assumption is dropped, observing one's own beliefs
is the only notion of observation available to a logical inductor.

minimum.

fields.action: Define a (P, U, V) optimal-policy notion and test it against counterfactual mugging, lizard world and decisionFlat_iff.

open-minded-epistemic-state.notes:
A candidate formalization filed by the session; nothing in the repository
develops it. The filing session reads it as the open-minded-updatelessness
question answered from the value side, with decisionFlat_iff a finite theorem
of the same shape.
open-minded-epistemic-state.source:
The maintainer's post Geometric UDT
(https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/Gmaq7vMj9NWLyQkEx/geometric-udt);
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/references/bli/chats/bli-chat-2024-12-09-udt-tiling-research-agenda.md,
turn 1 ("combining this with value uncertainty to justify something like
open-minded updatelessness").
open-minded-epistemic-state.statement:
An explicit epistemic state (P, U, V), with V a sub-sigma-algebra for value
uncertainty, carries a notion of optimal policy that yields updateless or
updateful behaviour in a counterfactual mugging according to which more
predictably serves the agent's true values, and is a distinct object from a
bargaining rule.

open-minded-updatelessness.author: @smithy-verity
open-minded-updatelessness.notes:
The sixth mid-level goal. The maintainer asks the question and names no
relation; 'endorsement-like' is the trust lab's framing, kept out of this
Statement. Open-minded updatelessness is Martín Soto's term; the LessWrong wiki

open-minded-updatelessness.source:
projects/deference/faf-cleanroom-2026-10-02/sources/unbounded-embedded/01-primary/summer-research-plan-2026--research-ideas-may-2026.md,
section Updatelessness (the maintainer, May 2026): "In a more updateless
context, are there any substantial ideas which characterize deference? Total
Trust isn't sufficient, or necessary. However, it isn't the case that UDT only
endorses its own exact prior, either. There are real improvements which UDT
will accept. Can we study what sort of "update" UDT will happily defer to?" and
"This would constitute significant progress on [open-minded
updatelessness](https://www.lesswrong.com/w/open-minded-updatelessness)."

turn 1: "Third, combining this with value uncertainty to justify something like
open-minded updatelessness. Figure out better ways to formally approach what to
be updateful about vs updateless about."
open-minded-updatelessness.statement:
A formal account says which updates an updateless agent accepts, what it is
updateful about and what updateless about, so that an updateless agent can
defer to a better-informed successor, by at least one of: a non-definitional
deference relation on the canonical examples; the coupling-graph
characterization of decision-flat refinements and its extension beyond pairwise
coupling; a superconditioning bridge from endorsement to evidence-indexed
policies.
